pages.title: Society rules
blocks: SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY RULES
1 NAME AND OBJECTIVES

The club shall be called the Southern English Setter Society (the Society),it is a non-profit making organisation formed solely for the benefits of its members. Its objective shall be to promote the breeding and exhibition, of pure English Setters in the Southern Counties of England; to urge the adoption of the published Kennel Club Standard for the breed on breeders and judges etc; to hold or to support Shows and Field Trials and to encourage the closest understanding between their promoters and breeders; to adopt such means as may be considered advisable for the improvement of the breed, by organised and concentrated effort to consolidate interest in English Setters.
2 OFFICERS AND COMMITTEE

The Society shall consist of Patron, President, Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Honorary Secretary, Honorary Treasurer who shall be ex-officio Members of the Committee, a Committee of fourteen and an unlimited number of Members.
No person whilst an undischarged bankrupt may serve on the Committee or hold other office or appointment within a Kennel Registered society.
3 COMMITTEE

The management of the Society shall be in the hands of a Committee consisting of fourteen Committee members and Six Officers. Meetings of the Committee shall be held as often as may be deemed necessary and five will form a Quorum for the transaction of the business. The Committee shall have the power to co-opt Members on to the Committee in the event of positions becoming vacant between Annual General Meetings. The Officers shall retire annually with half the Committee retiring bi-annually and shall be eligible for re-election. Members seeking election to the Committee shall have been Members of the Society for a minimum period of two years.
4 ELECTION OF MEMBERS
Candidates for Membership of the Society shall be proposed by one Member and seconded by another and elected by or balloted for by the Committee at one of its meetings, two negatives shall exclude.
5 VOTING AT MEETINGS
A duly elected member whose subscription is up to date will have one vote at all general meetings of the Society, Joint Members will each have one vote.
6 SUBSCRIPTIONS

The annual subscription payable to the Honorary Treasurer, shall be fixed sums (single or joint) to be agreed by the members at the AGM and due on the 1st October every year. No member whose subscription is unpaid shall be entitled to any privilege of the Membership and if any Member shall fail to pay the annual subscription by 1st March the Committee shall have the power to erase his / hers name from the list of members, but if the Committee shall subsequently receive a satisfactory explanation the member may, at the discretion of the Committee and on payment of arrears, be re-admitted to Membership.
7 SOCIETY PROPERTY
The property of the Society shall be vested in the Officers and Committee and in the event of the Society ceasing to exist, a General Meeting shall be called to decide the disposal of any assets.
8 EXPULSION OF MEMBERS

Any Member who shall be suspended under kennel Club Rule A42j(4) and or any Member whose dogs(s) is/are disqualified under kennel Club Rule A42j(8) shall ipso facto cease to be a Member of the Society for the duration of the suspension and or disqualification. If the conduct of any Member shall, in the opinion of the Committee of the Society, be injurious to the character or interests of the Society, the Committee of the Society may, at a meeting, the notice convening which includes as an object the consideration of the conduct of the Member, determine that a Special General Meeting of the Society be called for the purpose of passing a resolution to expel him / her. Notice of a Special General Meeting shall be sent to the accused member, giving particulars of the complaint and advising him / her of the place, date and hour of the meeting that he / she may attend and offer an explanation. If at the Meeting, a resolution to expel is passed by a two-thirds majority of the Members present and voting, his / her name shall forthwith be erased from the list of Members, and he / she shall thereupon cease for all purposes to be a Member of the Society except that he / she may within two calendar months from the date of such a meeting appeal to the Kennel Club upon and subject to such conditions as the Kennel Club impose.
9 ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
The Financial Year for the Society shall be – 1st January to 31st December.
The Annual General Meeting shall be held by 30th June next for the following purposes:-
1To receive the Report of the Committee and Balance Sheet
2 To elect the Officers and Committee.
3 To fix the subscription (Single or Joint / Overseas ) for the following year.

4 To discuss any resolution duly placed on the Agenda to which prior notice has been given to the Honorary Secretary. No Business shall be transacted at an Annual General Meeting unless notice thereof appears on the Agenda.
5 To discuss any other business normally conducted at an Annual General Meeting, or any matter which in the opinion of the Chairman of the Meeting is urgent.
The election of Officers and Committee at the Annual General Meeting shall be either by vote or ballot of those present at the Meeting.
10 SPECIAL MEETING

A Special Meeting shall be summoned by the Honorary Secretary if ten Members send a signed requisition stating the subject to be discussed; No business other than the matter on the Agenda can be discussed at a Special General Meeting.
11 NOTICE OF MEETINGS

At least twenty eight (28) days notice will be given of an Annual General Meeting, notice to be given to Members by publication in the dog press and a further notice will be published in at least fourteen (14) days before the Annual General Meeting. Agenda items should be forwarded at least twenty one (21) days before the Annual General Meeting. The Rules of the Society shall not be altered except at an Annual General Meeting or Special General Meeting. Any alterations to the rules shall not be brought into force until the Kennel Club has been advised and given its approval of the alterations.
12 SOCIETY ACCOUNTS

That banking accounts be opened in the name of the Society into which all revenue of the Society shall be paid and from which withdrawal shall only be made on the signature of any two of the Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer. The accounts shall be kept by the Treasurer and an Auditor shall be appointed at each Annual General Meeting who shall audit the Society's accounts for the ensuing year before the next Annual General Meeting.
13 MEMBERS LIST
The Society will make a list of Members and their addresses which will be available for inspection if so requested by the Members of the Society or by the Kennel Club.
14 JUDGES LIST

The Society will submit as part of ther Society's Annual Returns to the Kennel Club a copy of the English Setters Breed Clubs Joint List of Show Judges. The purpose of Breed Society Judging Lists is to indicate to all interested parties those persons a Breed Society would support at differing levels of judging. The list will be divided into three parts namely A1, A2,A3 and B. Membership of the Society must not be a prerequisite for inclusion in the list. A new list will be compiled by the Englisg Setter Joint Breed Clubs prior to the Annual General Meeting. All nominations for inclusion to the Judging List will be decided upon by the English Setter Joint Breed Clubs Committee.
15 SUBMISSION OF RETURNS TO THE KENNEL CLUB

The Officers acknowledge that during the month of January each year Maintenance of Title fee will be forwarded to the Kennel Club by the Secretary for the continuance of registration and that by 31st July each year, other returns, as stipulated by the Kennel Club Regulation for the Registration and Maintenance of Title of Societies and Breed Councils and Affiliation of Agricultural Societies and Municipal Authorities, will be forwarded to the Kennel Club. The Officers also acknowledge their duty to inform the Kennel Club of any changes of Secretary of the Society which may occur during the course of the year.
16 KENNEL CLUB THE FINAL COURT OF APPEAL
The Kennel Club shall be final Court of Appeal in all matters of dispute.
17 The Society shall not join any Federation of Societies or Clubs.

pages.title: warning xylitol
blocks: Subject: Xylitol Warning please pass on to ANYONE with pets!!!!
Only 3 grams of Xylitol (found in sugar free chewing gum) is enough to kill a 65lb dog. And QUICKLY!!!!! Please pass this warning on to everyone you know who has dogs. It may just save a life.
Here is the link to further information: http:// www.snopes.com/critters/crusader/xylitol.asp
Warning to all dog owners pass this on to everyone you can

Last Friday evening, I arrived home from work, fed Chloe, our 24 Lb dachshund, just as I normally do. Ten minutes later I walked into the den just in time to see her head inside the pocket of Katie's friend's purse. She had a guilty look on her face so I looked closer and saw a small package of sugar-free gum. It contained xylitol. I remembered that I had recently read that sugar-free gum can be deadly for dogs so I jumped on line and looked to see if xylitol was the ingredient. I found the first website below and it was the one. Next, I called our vet. She said to bring her in immediately. Unfortunately, it was still rush hour and it took me almost 1/2 hour to get there. Meanwhile, since this was her first case, our vet found another website to figure out the treatment. She took Chloe and said they would induce her to vomit, give her a charcoal drink to absorb the toxin (even though they don't think it works) then they would start an iv with dextrose. The xylitol causes dogs to secrete insulin so their blood sugar drops very quickly. The second thing that happens is liver failure. If that happens, even with aggressive treatment, it can be difficult to save them. She told us she would call us.

Almost two hours later, the vet called and said that contents of her stomach contained 2-3 gum wrappers and that her blood sugar had dropped from 90 to 59 in 30 minutes. She wanted us to take Chloe to another hospital that has a critical care unit operating around the clock. We picked her up and took her there. They had us call the ASPCA poison control for a case number and for a donation, their doctors would direct Chloe's doctor on treatment. They would continue the iv, monitor her blood every other hour and then in 2 days test her liver function. She ended up with a central line in her jugular vein since the one in her leg collapsed, just as our regular vet had feared.

Chloe spent almost the entire weekend in the critical care hospital. After her blood sugar was stabilized, she came home yesterday. They ran all the tests again before they released her and so far, no sign of liver damage. Had I not seen her head in the purse, she probably would have died and we wouldn't even had known wh y.

Three vets told me this weekend, that they were amazed that I even knew about it since they are first learning about it too. Please tell everyone you know about xylitol and dogs. It may save another life.

My thanks to the Officers and Committee for inviting me to judge the dogs at their Championship Show and for their warm hospitality. The new venue provided the benefit of generous sized rings and good lighting. I had many lovely dogs to go over but I have one main concern regarding mouths. BITCHES
Judge Sue Wilkinson

It was nice judging the breed again but feel that the overall quality is not what it used to be particularly in the puppy classes and this is where the breeding stock of the future lies. The Open Bitch was a tremendous class; the first four could change places any day. The feet on two third of the entry was appalling. No amount of roadwork will ever change bad feet. This is a fallacy. It is in the breeding, so do give this some consideration. Tails are another problem. They should be set almost in line with the back. Many were set on to low detracting from a level topline. There were not to many gay tails but the ones with them were those whose tails were set very low.

MINOR PUPPY (13.3) Difficult class to judge as they were all so naughty, but this is so much nicer than seeing them terrified, 1.Pearces Westonfields Pick A Lily mature eight month old blue, nice head, neck and shoulders, good all through, well muscled a little erratic on the move, but when she did settle she went well. 2.Frosts Tremorgan Blaze' Of Dreams pretty tricolour in good coat, pretty head, good neck and shoulders, well sprung ribs nice, not quite the feet of winner. 3.Bakers Mandyset The Futures Orange.

PUPPY (10. 5) 1.Hendersons Brenholm Spring Gift. 2, Bowens Brenholm Morning Sun At Chelmsett. I see they are litter sisters, Two very promising babies with lovely heads and expressions, both nicely made with good spring of rib and good feet. Both went well on the move, not a lot between them, but felt the winner was better in neck and was best puppy bitch. 3. Halsteads Hammoon Hidden Treasure.

VETERAN (4.2) 1 Halsteads Sh.Ch. Rockstro The-Night Fly Of Hammoon, very attractive dark blue who certainly deserves her title, lovely head, clean neck, good shoulders nice back end, good feet, really moved using her tail. 2. Jennings Canteris Conchita, a lot to like about her, was not so vivacious on the move

JUNIOR (15.6) 1 Bakers Mandyset Merry Go Round. I liked this tri, lovely head, good neck, shoulders bend of stifle, feet could be a little tighter, but stylish on the move when she settled. 2 Schonevilles Balvenie Marbree, pretty headed tri, very short coupled fore and aft, nice tail set, sound. 3. McCabe Rachdale Wild Flower.

SPECIAL YEARLING (5.2) I Colliers Bondgate Moment Of Madness At Rosarke, my type, prettv headed tri, lovely expression, dark eye, good neck shoulders and quarters, beautifully presented as are all from this, kennel, nice on the move. She has a bright. future. RCC. 2.Tompsetts Radbrooks Wouldn't It Be Nice difficult to go over as she was naughty, nice type, moved well.3,McCabes Rachdale Wild Flower.
MAIDEN 1 Bowens Brenhohn Morning Sun At Chelmset.
NOVICE (7.4) 1 Bakers Mandyset Merry Go Round 2. Jennings Capriata. 3. Aults Silversun Solstice Eve.

TYRO (5. 1) Buckleys Fishwick Maybe Baby. I liked her overall confirmation but found her a little plain in head. Very sound and won the class on her movement. 2.Tomsetts Radbrooks Wouldn't It Be Nice. 3.McCabes Rachdale Wild Flower.

GRADUATE (7.1) 1.Buckleys Fishwick Sunflower, orange, a true English, just my type, beautiful head and expression, presented to perfection, lovely on the move, tail set could be a little higher. 2.Reiths Elusive Secret Shadow, dark blue, a little out of coat but correctly constructed and moved well, not quite the head or expression of winner.3. Bartholomews Bartholeys Scarlet Ribbons.

POST GRADUATE (21.9) There were an awful lot of light eyes in this class. 1. Halsteads Hammoon Little Nutmeg. Not a big bitch but very sound. Sweet head, nice expression, good shoulders, well sprung ribs, not to long in loin. Immaculate as are all from this kennel. 2. Bakers Mandyset Jiggery Pokery, dark orange, nice head, expression, good reach of neck, good shoulders and bend of stifle, correct tail set. moved well using her tail. 3.Pearces Westonfields Honeysuckle.

LIMIT (12.5) 1. Wilkinson & Ludbrooks Beckantie Pipit. Very pretty headed dark blue, lovely dark eye, clean neck, well-laid shoulders, good quarters, sound mover. I liked her type. 2.Taylors & Searchs Bocharo Sapphire Blue of Wansleydale, dark blue, slightly rangier and not so mature as one, another nice type, moved well. 3.Kays Steelcross Blue Diamond.

OPEN (10. 5) 1. Morgan & Botts Roszarke Masquerade Behind Quensha. A beautiful headed tri with melting expression, long clean neck set into well-laid back shoulders. excellent spring of rib and not to long in loin, nice bend of stifle, correct tail set and feet. In lovely hard condition. I gave her the RCC when she was a junior and now she has matured she deserved her CC and Best In Show. Well done. 2. Cocketts SH.CH.Hollygrove Little White Lie. Blue. Another lovely bitch who certainly deserves her title. So much to like about her, and unfortunate to meet the winner. 3.Stubbingtons SH.CH. Bondgate Midnight Madness.
SPECIAL BEGINNERS (6.2) 1. Reiths Elusive Secret Shadow. 2.Tompsetts Radbrooks Wouldn't It Be Nice. 3.McCabes Rachdales Wild Flower.

BITCHES Judge Glenis Williams.

Thank you to SESS for the invitation and for making me so welcome. It is 5 years since I last judged the breed so all the bitches excluding veterans were new to me. I prefer to handle each exhibit so I an feel for construction rather than look on while a clever handler places legs etc. I am not a fault judge preferring to look for the positive attributes of the whole exhibit. I need to see and assess our lovely breed moving freely on a loose lead. From my entry I felt fronts are becoming a problem and there are still some ‘gay’ tails which for me spoils the topline. I was fortunate to have some top quality bitches to make my choices from particularly in the mature classes.

1. Golby’s Sorrodale She’s No Fool in Shadymore. 7 months tri, very much a baby, but pleasing in conformation, straight front, strong hindquarters, pleasing topline and tail carriage. Moved soundly when settled. Just needs to break in head and grow on.

Minor Puppy Dog 7 (1)

1. Dennis: Gemsett Dark Forces at Mariglen. Very balanced blue, correct in every way for age. Short coupled excellent bone, good feet, excellent topline, very appealing head and expression. Moved steadily and well.
2. Jones: Gemsett Gathering Fotce at Redbornstoke. Little brother of winner, very similar in most attributes, just slightly longer cast and not as balanced as yet. 3.Montgomery, Radlake Nijinsky
Puppy 11 Dog (2)

1. Morgan & Bott's Quensha Light My Fire. B.P.dog and BPIS. On a joint decision. Well put together orange, excellent sound mover front and aft with best of firm level toplines. Hard to fault, would just prefer a softer more expressive eye but overall quality made him outstanding in his class.

2.Day: Decovery Sandpiper. Slightly younger darker orange, smaller mould also oozes quality. Beautifully turned out showing of his elegant neck and shoulder line. Has got a lot going for him. 3. Young: Ingella Black Magic.
Veteran Dog 11

1. Wright: Wynacre Summer Gold. Orange, hard to believe 10 1/2 years old apart from some colour fading. Alert & active with a lovely head, soft appealing expression, obviously very at one with his handler. Still has a sound positive movement with a super head carriage. Good to see he still retains his good tight feet & full coat.
2.Devan: Carbine One Man. Lovely typy blue, giving away to age. Good head & kind soft expression, short coupled & well put together. Moved well & gave it his all. 3. Derry: Balvenie Paul Scarlet.
Junior Dog 3.(1).

1. Baker: Mandyset Prime Suspect. Very compact orange, appears smaller as he is very short in back and deep body. Most levely head & expression, excellent front assembly excellent in shoulders. Moved very well when he got his act together.

2. Young: Wansleydale Waterloo to Ingella. Blue, not the body of first, sweetest of heads, beautiful eye and expression. Gorgeous type of coat. I did not like the excess barbering of neck but that didn't influence my decision. Moved a little close behind.
Special Yearling Dog. 10.(1).

1. Littlechild & Davies:Ravensett Dark 'N' Dashing. Very smart and glamourous for such a dark blue. Excellent presentation & superb coat, Makes him a real eye catcher with much to like. Good depth & outline, head , expression & best of feet.

2.Mitchell: Tattersett Drummer Boy. Another lesson in presentation, pleasing head, good neck, a little upright behind so looking long in hock but moved positively & steadily, well deserved his place. 3. Cooper: Tremorgan Prince of Wales at Settrenda
Novice Dog 8
1.Repeat. Baker: Mandyset Prime Suspect:2. Repeat Day: Decovery Sandpiper. 3. Repeat Young: Wansleydale Waterloo to Ingella
Tyro Dog. 4.
1.Land: Tattersett Firebird. Orange, pleasing head, good overall appearance, slightly upright in front and looking immature.
2.Forman: Somoray pioneer. Slightly built blue, pleasing but a little upright in front. Good sweep of stifle & good level back & tail set.
Graduate Dog 10 (3)

1:Stephenson:Wistaston School Timesaver for Steeplow. Very appealing young orange, not a large one but well proportioned & balanced. Pleasing head with a kind eye & expression, looking a little cut up in loin at present but he is young with good potential. Well presented & handled
2.Repeat Mitchell: Tattersett Drummer Boy. 3. Dobbie: Moorbrook Prime Time
Post Graduate Dog 13 (4)
1. Derry: Balvenie What a Sensation. Young wery elegant orange, attractive head, masculine but not over-done, super expression, excellent clean neck & shoulder line, good positive steady mover.
2. Richards: Rubuscott Its All Over Now. Very dark blue, pleasing head, soft expression, well presented, good neck & shoulder line, level top line & good stifle.3.Young: Ingella Prarie Gold
Limit Dog 17 (4)
Superb class, dominated by two outstanding dogs. As I looked around I experienced the 'wow factor'. Hard to separate but on the day the winner had just the edge in sparkle.

1. Swannell: Rickory rave Review. Superb elegant blue with seemingly everything in the right place. Racy yet substantial quality refined head, deep chested, well ribbed, his outline flowed in all lines. delighted to award him I gather his third CC and thrilled on referees decision to make him B.O.B. & Best in Show.

2. Wale: Wansleydale Storm Magic. Narrowly beaten, another totally balanced elegant orange. Sure they will change places many times. I would be proud to own either - and preferably both. 3 . Mellish: Ownways Moving Shadow of Monbrec.
Open Dog 17 (4)
I have not seen a star-studded class like this in years, my decisions were almost by splitting hairs. None need much comment form me.
1. Williams: Sh Ch Bournehouse Royal Colours. RCC. Lovely type in full coat. He had to be special to win this class

2. Dennis: Sh Ch Wistaston School Breeze at Elswood. Another beatifully worthy title holder with exquisite head & expression to die for. Just lacking a little in furnishings to complete the picture. 3.Grimsdell: Tattersett Stockbroker
Special Beginner 3
1. Jolley: Bellesett Masterpiece of Jollymore. Orange, good dark eye, appealing head, level top line, would prefer slightly heavier bone.
2. Alexander: Merleycopse Perfect Gent of Alexator. Nice headed blue, happy to show, looking very immature and out of coat at present. 3.Reith: Mandyset Dirty Dancing.
June Reed

pages.title: show critique
blocks: Go to Dogs
SESS CHAMPIONSHIP SHOW BITCHES Bitch Judge Mrs Jackie Thorburn (Atlasta)
I should like to offer my sincere apologies for the delay in this critique.
My thanks go to the Committee for running an efficient show with a lovely atmosphere.

To the exhibitors an additional thank you for your entries and for braving the awful weather. It was a quality entry and many of the youngsters that need time to settle into showing will indeed have their day.

MINOR PUPPY BITCH. 1 Rosetimber Foxy Lady - Dark mild eye of correct shape. Well defined stop for age. Good reach of neck into well laid back shoulders. Good hind angulation. 2. Westonfields April Showers - Level top line maintained on the move. Slightly more strength to forearm would give tighter front end.

PUPPY BITCH . 1.Quensha Tears of Pearls - Mature for age. Well boned. Balanced head with beep muzzle and well defined stop. 2. Ownways Touch N Dry - Finer built than winner but very feminine. Excellent topline with good tail set. Moved gracefully around the ring. 3. Bondgate Evening Star over Mariglen.

VETERAN BITCH. This class has always given me pleasure to judge. It is from these ladies that the winners of today are made.1. Bensophie Miss Melion - Best Veteran - Balanced bitch of substance and in excellent coat. Dark eye. Covered the ground effortlessly. A picture of elegance and femininity in her senior years. 2. Bournehouse Harvest gold - Close up to winner. Same remarks apply. Held her topline on the move with slashing tale and was obviously enjoying her day out. 3. Roszarke First Love at Decoverly.

JUNIOR. 1 Llinlow Monets Garden via Rockstro - Without being flashy a quality bitch which I am sure will have a bright future. Substantial bitch for here age yet maintaining her femininity. Balanced and well boned. Despite being moved by a separate handler constantly moved with drive and style. 2. Ravenset Annique at Wolmersdon - Another good head with gentle expression and correct ear set. Drove from the hock on the move maintaining a level topline. Not as tight in front as the winner.3. Richecca Party Coulurs for Radbrooks

YEARLING. 1.llinlow Monets garden. 2. Richecca Role Model at Rickory - Another quality bitch which this kennel is known for, not the work in the head of the winner of the class and generally lighter in build. Good reach of neck and correctly angulated. Well handled, 3. Hannadene Mollly Malone.
MAIDEN. 1. Llinlow Monets Garden. 2. Bondgate Evening Star over Mariglen - Very pretty bitch. Short coupled and deep in brisket. 3. Quensha Truly Madly Deeply.

NOVICE. 1. Llinlow Monets Garden - 2. Quensha Truly Madly deeply - A truly lovely bitch. Dark eye and just the right amount of work in her head with square muzzle and low ear set. Straight front and tight feet. Needs to settle on the move, It was nice to see the handler not expecting to much from her. She will achieve as she matures and settles.3 Ravensett Dark N Delicious with Thistlesett
TYRO. 1. Llinlow Monets Garden. 2. Mandyset Ready Stready Go - Not a big bitch. Sound and a bundle of energy on the move! Good hind angulation. 3. Culverwell Rhapsody in Blue..

GRADUATE. 1. Halliana Dancing Queen - Elegant balanced outline. Strong muscular neck into well laod back shoulders. Has a tendancy to crab. 2. Phenset Three Wishes for Ferrygate - pleasing bitch. Not the conformation of the first. Out of coat. I personally should like to see her less severely trimmed.

POST GRADUATE. 1. Daraquist Maid in Devon - sound bitch. Excellent work in head with dark eye. Another kennel from which one has learnt to expect quality. Good rear angulation and drove well from the hock on the move. Elegant.2. Lewkins Wide Load Winnie at Frizzanti - Her name does not do her justice! Another quality bitch with good front end and tight feet. In good hard condition. Soft feminine expression. Sadly lacking coat. Covered the ground effortlessly, 3. Fishwick Queen of the Night at Quensha.

LIMIT. 1. Bondgate Utter Madness. Reserve CC - Long muscular neck into well set apart shoulders. Good beep brisket and well rounded chest. An extremely excellent outline which she never lost on the move. Good tail set which she used with a lovely slashing movement.2. Hammoon Firefly - Close up to the winner. Beautifully defined head.3. Westonfield Honysuckle.

OPEN. 1. Sh CH Wansleydale Blackbird CC and Best in Show - what a stummer and an amazing show girl. In hard condition and full coat. Excellent work to the head. Dark eye, correct ear set and depth of muzzle. For me perdectly constructed which won her a deserved best in show.2. Sh CH Fishwick Sunflower - Good overall balance and clean outline. Lovely head and expressive eye. Very impressive on the move. 3. Hannadene Masqurade at Joldeane.
SPECIAL BEGINNERS. 1.Fenston Dance Du Due - pleasing bitch. Nice kind expression. A little more work needed on her movement. 3. Tattersett Demure.
SESS CHAMPIONSHIP SHOW 2005 DOGS Dog Judge Mrs J Barlow (Sondrew)

The Southern English Setters Society held a Championship Show at North Tidworth on 20th Nov 2005, where it was an honour to be invited to Judge the Dogs. All top placings were made in agreement with my Co-Judge Mrs J. Thorburn. BIS was Taylor's bitch Sh.Ch. Wansleydale Blackberry. RBIS was Derry's Sh.Ch. Balvenie What A Sensation, with BP going to Stubbington Buckley's Bondgate Single Malt.

MINOR PUPPY DOG. 1.Holland's Earldoms Whispering Forest. 7months orange with pleasing head and good shoulders, length of neck, compact body, looked nice standing and moved steadily. Still very much a baby. 2. Cozens' Earldoms Bold Forester. litter brother to first, Tri with good head & expression. Good body and nicely angulated rear. Not so clean in neck and shoulders as 1. Movement not quite together at the moment.

PUPPY DOG 1.Stubbington & Buckley's - Bondgate Single Malt 7months Orange. Handsome puppy with a good head, kind expression, good bone, length of leg, good shoulders - hind angulation, moved soundly, still has a lot of maturing to do as one would expect at his age, but his type and soundness won him this place and BPIS. 2 . Ball's Bondgate Wayward Lad From Beaverhill (NAF),loveley tri, litter brother to 1. Very similar in type and quality. In lovely coat and condtion. Moved and handled well: 3. Gilbert 's Quensha To The Moon and Back at Shadowood

VETERAN DOG ( (4). 1. Dunks - Sh Ch Samelen Shooting Star 8yr old blue, moved and showed like a youngster. Super head and expression, good shoulders and depth of chest, level topline moving and standing. Has retained his quality and condition. A credit to his owner. 2. Harradine's - Halliana Dashing Blue. Even at 9years lives up to his name , lovely old boy, good head and lay of shoulders, nice depth of rib, still in good condition, strong quarters. Moved with grace and style. 3. Beckwith's - IR/DUTCH/LUX Sh Ch Tattersett Time is Time

Class 4 . JUNIOR DOG 6(1) 1. Wale's - Wansleydale Magic Star JW. What a beautiful orange dog this is, shows all the essentials and quality of this breed. Lovely in profile, noble head carriage with good reach of neck. Good angulation with width and depth of rib, strong quarters. Moved at one with his handler, missed out on RCC by a whisker. His day will surely come. 2. Sykes' - Wandsfell Leading Me Astray at Daraquist. Another lovely orange, slightly smaller all round than 1. Quality dog compares very well to the standard, good head and shoulders, well balanced body and well angulated quarters. Super mover retaining balance and style.: 3. Barber's - Llinlow Trouble at Bay

YEARLING DOG 8(1). 1. Taylor's - Wandsleydale Witch Doctor. Litter brother to Junior winner so same remarks apply, not quite as big but I think he will make the same impact in the future as he matures. His overall quality and presentation won him this good class. 2. Schoneville's - Mariglen Get Carter at Balvenie JW. Slightly larger than 1 but very close decision. Good outline and balance, well constructed, good bone without being overdone, lovely head and in good coat and condition. Moved well holding his topline. 3. Sykes' - Wandsfell Leading Me Astray at Daraquist:

MAIDEN DOG 3(1) 1. Critchell - Imms' - Tattersett Smokescreen, Tri dog of good proportions. Good coat, bone, and shoulders, well angulated hind quarters. Moved O.K. 2. Burgess' - Jawontie Touched by the Sun. Nice orange. Preferred his head to 1 so a close decision, slighty smaller but in proportion. Good head with gentle expression, long neck and good body. Moved well.

NOVICE DOG 1.Taylor's - Wandsleydale Witch Doctor: 2 .Henry - Beechanger Golden Cricket. Good orange with clean outline, super reach of neck, deep brisket and well angulated hind quarters. Moved well, would like a bit more weight. 3 .Critchell - Imms' - Tattersett Smokescreen

TYRO DOG 3. 1 .Taylor's - Wandsleydale Witch Doctor: 2 .Beckwith's - Swannery Zeus. My notes say naughty Tri dog but lovely whan standing still. Good shaped head with dark eye, good shoulders, compact body. A lively happy lad. 3 .Malins' - Taurkel Gold Quest.

GRADUATE DOG 5(3) 1 .Wells' - Holygrove Storyteller at Ritanor. 2 .Stubbington's - Bondgate Mr Nice Guy. A hard decision between these two. Both well constructed and fitting the standard, lovely heads, long necks and good shoulders. Very similar in height and length and overall soundeness. Both moved well but 1 was carrying the correct weight which gave him the class.

10 POST GRADUATE DOG 15(1). 1 .Day's - Decoverly Celtic Venture. This tri dog took my eye with his overall balance and soundness in a strong class of differing types. This was the dog I would take home. Pleasing head shape and proportions, kind alert expression, good shoulders short coupled with correct rear angulation, well muscled and in hard condition. Looked well in final line up which gave him RCC. 2 .Holland's - Mandyset Dirty dancing. Blue who needs to be gone over to be appreciated. Well made all through, balanced profile, good head with reachy neck in well placed shoulders, short coupled, strong over the loin and backend. Move well: 3 Stubbington's - Bondgate Mr Nice Guy .

11 LIMIT DOG 9(1). 1. Hill & Littlechild's - Ravensett American Gigolo at Somerled JW. A favourite of mine who looked at his best today. Eye catching dark blue who showed well. Best of heads, not overdone, generally well constructed throughout, beep body with good spring of rib, well balanced, super outline when moving and in profile. 2. Day's - Decoverly Sandpiper. Super orange of substance and style. An outstanding dog, mature and refined without exageration. Liked his body properties and sound quarters. In excellent coat and condition. Move and showed well. 3. Cooper's - Tremorgan Prince of Wales to Settrenda.

OPEN DOG 10(1) 1. Derry's - Sh Ch Balvinie What a Sensation. What a beautiful dog this is. Best of heads with gentle expression, so well made all through. Balanced outline, straight front with good shoulders, angulation, deep strong body with nicely sprung ribs, well built quarters. Covers the ground with style and elegance. Pleased to award him the CC.: 2. Littlechild & Davis' - Sh Ch Ravensett Dark 'n' Dashing JW. Handsome dark blue, worthy champion. Compact, short coupled, nice depth of body with no excess weight, lovely type. Has lots of quality without being overdone, balanced outline held on the move. Shown in excellent coat and condition. 3. Mellish's - Ownways Moving Shadow for Monbrec

SPECIAL BEGINNERS DOG 4(2) 1. Critchell - Imms' - Tattersett Smokescreen: 2. Jolly's - Belleset Masterpiece of Jolymore. Orange with nice head and eye. Longer cast than 1, good shoulders and well angulated quarters. Moved O.K.
J.A.Barlow (Judge)

Bitches

Minor Puppy Bitch (3.1A) . 1st & BP. Hartle's Hartsett Love Sonnet, 6months lovely light blue, good reach of neck, would prefer more angulation to upper arm, well bodied for age with strong hindquarters, lovely coat and condition. 2nd Christian's Winterpick All About Reo. 7month orange sweet head with darker eye than winner but not so together, moving and feet not good. Good body and coat, both moved well for age.

Puppy Bitch (3). 1st Baker's Mandyset Only a Caution, 11 months. Blue with a good head, neck and shoulders, excellent body with strong hindquarters, nice tight feet, Rather erratic moving. 2nd Watkin's Albadora Starlite Everglow of Valsett. 9months. Blue with good neck, body and quarters, not as much angulation to upper arm and lighter eye than winner.3rd. Bridgeman's Mandyset Ice Lady.

Veteran (3.2A). 1st Harris's Mariglen Fallin For A Dancer with Gemsett. RES CC. 8yrs Dark blue, most beautiful head with dark eyes, excellent reach of neck, good front with well-angled upper arm, strong hindquarters with good bend of stifle and well let down hocks. If she had only co-operated with her handler might have taken top honours.2nd Harradine's Halliana Petite Fleur. 8yrs. Lighter blue not front or feet of winner but showed and moved well for age.

Junior (6,2A). 1st Tomsett's Radbrooks Wild Honey. Orange nice head with good length of neck, fairly good front and body depth, longer cast than second but better hindquarters. 2nd Izzard and Barton's Tattersett read All About It. Very dark blue, beautiful head and expression, short coupled with good front and feet. 3rd Hartle's Hartsett Ruby Sunrise.

Yearling (1). 1st Harris and Dennis's Bondgate Evening Star over Mariglen. Tri Lovely head, good length of neck fairly good front, rather long cast and would prefer more rugged hindquarters. In Excellent condition.
Maiden (5). 1st Izzards and Barton's Tattersett Read All About It. 2nd Watkin's Albadora Starlite Everglow of Valsett. 3rd Harris's Walshaw Moondust.
Novice (2) 1st Izzards and Barton's Tattersett Read All About It.2nd Bridgeman's Mandyset Welcome Return.Tri. Not front or feet of winner and longer cast, but good deep body and really well muscled.

Graduate (4.1A) 1st Wyatt's Culverwell Rhapsody in Blue. Lovely head and expression, good front, body and quarters, nice tight feet, carrying far too much weight. 2nd Tompsett's Richecca Party Colours for Radbrooks. Orange. Sweet head and expression not the front or coat of winner and longer cast. 3rd Salmon's Rechecca Fancy Colours,

Post Graduate (9.1A). 1st Montgomery's Radlake Firebird. Tri. Unfortunately left her coat at home, but pleased me enough to win the class with her lovely head and expression. Excellent front end and quarters. Good body and dear little tail which is a rare thing nowadays. 2md Morgan's Mariglen Steals the Heart of Meandi. Tri. Lovely head good reach of neck. Good depth of body but much longer cast than winner, good feet and lovely coat.3rd Croft's Ravensett Dark'N'Delicious with Thistlesett.

Limit (14.5A). 1st Schoneville and Derry's Balvenie Mary Rose JW. Dark blue with a lovely head, good reach of neck, deep body with well-sprung ribs, good front and short coupled with strong hindquarters. Could have better feet in excellent coat and condition. 2nd Oliver's Wansleydale Songbird at Bramstorm. Tri. Lovely head and expression. Good body and quarters, slightly shorter in upper arm than winner, both moved well. 3rd Gilbert's Mariglen Steals The Show at Shadowood.

Open (7.3A). 1st & CC and Res BIS. Dennis's Sh Ch Fenston Arabella at Mariglen. Orange. In superb coat with a lovely head good reach of neck. Fully matured in body, excellent front and quarters, carrying enough weight and unfortunately a dead tail but still thought her worthy of the ticket. 2nd Attwood's Sh CH Swannery Golden Valentine. Orange. Sweet head and expression, good reach of neck, not the coat or feet of winner, and slightly longer cast. 3rd Cozens's Earldoms Destinys Child.

Special Beginners (6.3A). 1st Henderson's Jawonte Tonight & Forever. Tri. Nice head, good body, coat and condition, better front than second but longer cast. 2nd Salmon's Fenston Danse Du Feu. Dark Tri. Pretty head and expression much shorter coupled than winner but not the front or quarters, In good coat and condition. 3rd Salmon's Richecca Fancy Colours.
Jean Parsons (Judge)

pages.title: show critique
blocks: Southern English Setter Society Championship Show 19 November 2006
English Setter (Dogs)
Judge Mr Steve Collier (Roszarke)

The SESS committee ran a well organised show with a friendly atmosphere, making it a very enjoyable show to judge. It was good to see some quality puppies coming through and a depth of quality in the older classes. The principle winners were agreed jointly with my co-judge Mrs Parsons; BIS was the dog Valsett Starlite Shine On, RBIS was the bitch Sh.Ch. Fenston Arabella At Mariglen, and BPIS was the dog Mariglen Pengtsson's Legacy.
Minor Puppy Dog - 5 entries (2 absent)

1. Hammond's Hartsett Going For Gold With Oaktrish - Young puppy with balanced head and pleasing expression. Shown in good condition, well bodied up, with level top line and good tail set. Moved steadily with straight front and good rear drive. 2. Wright's Fishwick Dancing Lad - Not as mature as the winner and needs more time to settle. Lean balanced head with dark eye and soft expression. Excels in good reach of neck and correct lay-back of shoulder. Needs time to tighten on move. 3. Williams Winterpick Wots It About
Puppy Dog - 3 entries

1. Dennis's Mariglen Pengtsson's Legacy - Outstanding young blue dog, showing a great deal of promise, elegant in appearance, balanced throughout, short coupled and shown in excellent coat and condition. Masculine head with the right amount of work and dark eye making a very attractive young boy. Good reach of neck with clean shoulders and level top line. Straight front and good rear movement, used his tail well and good head carriage. Pleased to see him go best puppy in show. 2. Blackie's Taggleshaw Royal Ensign Over - Promising puppy that still needs time to mature. Good round bone and balanced outline, balanced head with dark eye making a soft expression. Needs to tighten on move. 3. Thompson's Samelen Jupiter
Veteran Dog - 5 entries (2 absent)

1. Harradine's Halliana Dashing Blue - 10 year old veteran dog, still in good coat and condition, and willing to show for his owner. Good reach of neck with correct lay-back of shoulders, short in back with level top line, and good tail set, making a balanced outline. Good positive movement with slashing tail and high head carriage. Went on to win best veteran in show following referee's decision. 2. Mellish's Ownway's Moving Shadow For Monbrec - Another veteran dog happy to be in the ring and showed well for his owner. Clean over lean neck and well laid back shoulders, level top line and good tail-set. Balanced head with dark eye and soft expression. Good round bone and straight on move, moved steadily. 3. Sayers Cumbersett Raven Rebel of Christter
Junior Dog - 7 entries

1. Tucker's Walshaw Moonstorm - Well balanced dog with good conformation and everything in proportion. Straight in front, tight feet, level top line and strong rear quarters. Masculine lean head with dark eye and soft expression. Steady true movement with happy slashing tail. 2. Neath's Albadora Shadow Boxer - Dark blue dog that didn't catch the eye at first glance, but surprised on closer examination. Excelled in neck and shoulders with correct lean head and dark eye making an appealing expression. Shown in good coat and condition. Good rear quarters, providing overall balance. I preferred the top line and movement of 1 on the day. 3. Cole's Sorbus Looks Could Kill
Special Yearling Dog - 3 entries

1. Gilbert's Quensha To The Moon And Back At Shadowwood - Balanced orange dog well bodied with level top line, strong bone and deep brisket. Straight front moved using his tail well. Good reach of neck and clean over shoulders. 2. Bates Tudorfield Blue Lightening - Shown in good coat and condition with level top line and well set-on tail. Elegant lean head with dark eye. Steady on the move, straight at both front and rear. Would have preferred deeper brisket for more heart room. 3. Lenzi's Pilsdon Jack-A-Dandy
Maiden Dog - 5 entries

1. Tucker's Walshaw Moonstorm - won Junior dog 2. Baker's Mandyset First Offence - A very close decision between 1 and 2. Moved true with purpose and drive. Good round bone, level in top line and good tail set. I preferred the head of 1 on the day. 3. Neath's Albadora Shadow Boxer
Novice Dog - 6 entries
1. Tucker's Walshaw Moonstorm - won Junior and Maiden dog 2. Baker's Mandyset First Offence - 2nd in Maiden dog 3. Cozens Earldoms Bold Forester
Tyro Dog - 4 entries

1. Ball's Bondgate Wayward Lad From Beaverhill - Good size dog shown in good coat and condition. Elegant head and expression and excels in reach of neck and lay-back of shoulder. Straight front, tight feet and level top line. Moved with drive with happy slashing tail. 2. Cozens Earldoms Bold Forester - Smaller dog than 1, with balanced outline and true movement. Good conformation with level top line and well set-on tail. Lean head with dark eye and soft expression 3. Wright's Wynacre Born To Dance
Graduate Dog - 5 entries (1 absent)

1. Kirsch's Soul Mate Of Sorbus - Blue dog shown in excellent condition. Clean in outline with everything in proportion. Excelled in conformation with good reach of neck and clean shoulders, level top line and good tail set. Good round bone with tight feet and straight front. Moved with drive, slashing tail and correct head carriage. Lean masculine head with dark eye and soft expression. Pushed hard for RCC 2. Mellish's Harvancourt In Touch With Moonbrec - Balanced outline with good neck and shoulders. Lean head with dark eye and good expression. Strong rear quarters and steady true movement. 3. Neath's Albadora Born Lucky
Post Graduate Dog - 10 entries (3 absent)

1. Tucker's Walshaw Party With Me - Very close decision between 1 and 2. Both dogs shown in good coat and condition and have balanced outlines with good reach of neck and clean shoulders. I preferred the head of 1 on the day.1st moved true with straight front and strong rear quarters. Lovely tight feet and good bone, dark eyes and appealing expression. 2. Stubbington's Bondgate Mr Nice Guy - Very similar attributes to 1. I'm sure they will change places on a regular basis. Tri dog with super top line and tail set giving a clean overall picture. Moved well with slashing tail. Lean head with dark eye and soft expression. 3. Malins Taukel Gold Quest
Limit Dog - 10 entries (2 absent)

1. Wells Hollygrove Story teller At Ritanor - Elegant blue dog with balanced outline and good conformation. Excels in neck and shoulders with good reach and correct lay-back. Level top line and good tail set. Masculine head with appealing expression. Shown in excellent coat and condition. Straight front. Moved freely with natural high head carriage and good driving rear action using his tail correctly. Pleased to award RCC; should go on to become a show champion. 2. McCabe's Rachdale Wind Bird - Mature orange dog I have liked and judged well before and who pushed hard for first place. Shown in excellent coat and condition, Masculine head good top line making a balanced picture throughout and moved with correct head carriage. Today I preferred the elegance and free movement of 1 3. Schoneville's Mariglen Get Carter Balvenie
Open Dog - 11 entries (6 absent)

1. Watkin's Valsett Starlite Shine On - Elegant in appearance, balanced throughout, short coupled and shown in excellent coat and condition. Beautiful lean head with dark eye and appealing expression. Good angulation both front and rear, straight in front and strong rear quarters. Moved true and with purpose. Had the extra sparkle on the day to win the CC. Pleased to see him go BIS 2. Derry's Sh.Ch. Balvenie What A Sensation - Balanced throughout with good body properties and shown in excellent coat and condition. Moved happily with straight front movement and good rear drive. I preferred the head and expression of 1 today 3. Harradine's Wildquest Samba Spirit Of Halliana
Sp. Beginners Dog - 2 entries

1. Mellish's Harvancourt In Touch With Moonbrec - 2nd in Graduate dog 2. Burgess's Jawonte Touched By The Sun - Shown in good coat and condition, happy mover with straight front and good rear angulation. Preferred the neck and shoulders of 1 today

pages.title: show critique 2007
blocks: THE SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY
BREED CHAMPIONSHIP SHOW
NORTH TIDWORTH, WILTSHIRE 18th NOVEMBER 2007
ENGLISH SETTERS
BITCHES
Firstly, apologies for taking so long to have the following uploaded to the web having now returned to my secretarial duties.

I would like to thank all exhibitors for presenting their exhibits in such clean condition but I was perturbed to see some upright shoulders and high carried tails that spoilt the chances of some otherwise good exhibits.

Minor Puppy (5: 1) 1. Littlechild's RAVENSETT DARK SECRETS An 8 month old dark B/B & tan full of type, very pretty feminine head with the darkest of eye, arched neck into well-laid shoulders super forehand and rear angulation, looked as if she enjoyed herself on the move. Will follow this youngster's development with interest. 2. Baker's MANDYSETT MIND YOUR MANNERS Head lean with plenty of work for one so young, lovely balance, good head shape with dark eye and sweet expression , well bodied, excellent construction from nose to tail, a happy mover. 3. Henry's BEECHANGER LITTLE SHREW

Puppy (3: 0 ) 1. Dennis and Field's MARIGLEN FRANCESCA FENSTON . Well developed 9 month old light O/B ,very mature for her age, a most beautiful head and expression , so balanced, super angulation fore and aft, deep body, good spring of rib, short coupled and level topline which she held whilst moving freely covering the ground with drive. Presented in tip top condition and handled to perfection, BP and in agreement with my co-judge pleased to award her Best Puppy in Show. 2. Davis' CULVERWELL CALYPSO OF MERLEYCOPSE 10 month old O/B A little unsettled today and giving her handler a hard time but none the less a lot to like about this young lady, head of good shape, dark eye, long neck into well laid shoulders, level back and good tail set, strong bone and tight feet. Not as steady as 1 on the move. 3. Cozens' LARRENIE BONNIE LASS FOR EARLDOMS

Veteran (3:2) 1. Bates's TUDORFIELD BLUE ANGEL A seven 1/2 year old B/B and how she seemed to enjoy her day. standing with an aloof air and movement that would put many a youngster to shame. Appealing head, good neck and shoulders well ribbed and short in loin well angulated rear end that drove well when moving so soundly.

Junior (8:2) 1. Schoneville and Derry's FANTAILS JUST GEORGIA VOOR BALVENIE (IMP) A really super youngster, beautiful chiselled head with darkest of eye, superb construction, well angled forehand, strong bone and pasterns, well sprung rib cage and deep in the back rib, driving hindquarters moved with drive and enthusiasm, maturing nicely, another one to watch for the future. 2 .Richard DECOVERLY SWEET CAROLINE WITH RUBUSCOTT Pretty O/B with sweet head, strong neck arched into good shoulders, deep compact body, didn't move as steady as 1. 3 .Baker's MANDYSETT WHAT A DI' MOND

Yearling (3:0) 1. Schoneville and Derry's FANTAILS JUST GEORGIA VOOR BALVENIE (IMP) 2. Golby and Deacon's SHADYMOORE PRYD 'N' PREJUDICE O/B Well proportioned head with a melting expression, deep chest, well ribbed up and level topline, overall a good sound bitch who moved well driving off her hocks. 3. Baker's MANDYSETT WHAT A DI'MOND
Maiden (1:0) 1. Richards' DECOVERLY SWEET CAROLINE WITH RUBUSCOTT

Novice (6: 3) 1. Richards' DECOVERLY SWEET CAROLINE WITH RUBUSCOTT . 2. Oliver's WANSLEYDALE CLOUDBERRY AT BRAMSTORM A very feminine dark B/B & tan with lovely outline when stood, good forehand conformation, well ribbed up with well muscled and angulated hindquarters, moved well, beautifully handled and presented. 3. Bridgeman's MANDYSET WELCOME RETURN

Tyro (5:2) 1. Harris' WALSHAW MOONDUST B/B with a gorgeous head and expression soft expression and dark eye enhanced with low ear set and an eye patch. Long reachy and arched neck, level topline and good tailset On the move drove of strong hind quarters with soundness and style. 2. Reith's OWNWAYS TOUCH N TELL Another well constructed bitch pleasing head and forehand assembly with level back and good hind angulation, needs a bit more coat . Just preferred the outline of 1 on the move. 3. Bridgeman's MANDYSET WELCOME RETURN

Graduate (6:3) 1. Deering's ROSETIMBER FOXY LADY A very pretty B/B who when settled began to show herself, beautiful head shape, dark eye and most appealing expression, deep flew and good stop, well arched neck flowing into well laid shoulders, good bone and strong pasterns, driving hindquarters, maturing nicely. 2. Bartholomew's SWANNERY TEAR DROP FOR BARTHOLEYS Light B/B, Another lovely bitch, not quite the head of 1 but super overall conformation moved with drive and well handled and presented in hard condition. 3. Montell's CULVERWELL SUMMER COLOURS

Post Graduate (9:3) 1. Day's MANDYSET READY STEADY GO TO DECOVERLY O/B Not a large bitch but oozes quality from her beautiful head with the softest of expressions to the tip of her wagging tail. An excellent forehand good depth of brisket and spring of rib, short coupled with strong well angled and muscular hindquarters moved with real drive. 2. Cockett's HOLLYGROVE SECRET LOVE An attractive B/B who has so many attributes, her conformation is so sound and although she moved steady didn't really have the sparkle today. 3. Bartholomew's TATTERSETT MYSTIC DREAM AT BARTHOLEYS

Limit (10:3) 1. Harris' MARIGLEN PRINCESS ROYAL AT GEMSETT Beautifully presented showing a balanced picture, soft melting expression with plenty of work in the head, long lean arched neck into well laid shoulders, short back, well ribbed with level topline and super tailset , powerful true and steady driving movement . 2. Hewitt's TATTERSETT DEMURE Another lovely lady elegant and stylish, put down to perfection in lovely coat and hard condition , good overall conformation, moved soundly with free flowing action. 3. Furze's TREGMORGAN DADDY'S GIRL

Open (12:4) 1. Grimsdell's Sh Ch TATTERSETT COLOURS JW A beautiful light B/B & tan bitch so worthy of her title. Balanced and elegant, well constructed in all departments, lovely arched neck into well laid back shoulders, level topline held on the move, stylish driving mover with slashing tail in full coat and feather presented in immaculate condition , proud to award her the CC. R BiS . 2. Watkin's VALSETT STARLITE STARSHINE Another gorgeous bitch plenty of work in the head dark eye and well arched neck. Strong round bone & upright pasterns, Well bodied, strong quarters with great bend of stifle. Moved well using her slashing tail all the time. In good coat and hard condition. unlucky to meet 1 today in such form. RCC . 3. Oliver's WANSLEYDALE SONGBIRD AT BRAMSTORM

Special Beginners (6:3) 1. James' INGELLA PINCH OF NUTMEG Light O/B Reserve in a strong Post Grad class a very attractive and well balanced orange bitch, pretty head, well bodied, good depth and spring of rib, short coupled with good angulation fore and aft, moved steady. 2. Hewitt's TATTERSETT DOUBLE ACTION A raw youngster placed vhc in a good Junior class, has all the parts in the right place just needs time to mature. Moved well for one so young. 3. Reith's OWNWAYS TOUCH N TELL
Dave Lewis (Judge)
DOGS

I felt privileged to have been invited to judge the dogs at this prestigious show. Mouths on the whole were good but shoulders still cause me concern as does the hind movement action in many dogs which resulted in a few otherwise good dogs been penalised.

Minor Puppy ( 2 0 ) 1 Barlow's Mandysett Mind Over Matter 7 month orange, pleasing head and expression, good body properties for its age, level top line, stifles well bent, quite steady on the move for a youngster. 2 Bates' Tudorfield Goes Forth a six month old orange baby pleasing in outline, good bone and well angulated hindquarters, not as steady as one on the move.

Puppy ( 1 1 ) 1 Montell's Culverwell Flashman although standing alone this 19 month tri was well worth his first placing, attractive head, dark eye, good in front, well sprung ribs and bend of stifle, good coat for a youngster and moved soundly. Best Puppy Dog.

Veteran ( 3 0 ) 1 Jolley's Bellesett Masterpiece of Jolymore nine year old orange shown in good coat, pleasing overall shape, attractive head, straight front and firm rear quarters, moved correctly and pleased, with my co-judge to award him Best Veteran in Show. 2 Mellish's Ownways Moving Shadow For Monbrec a well made blue dog, pleasing in head and expression, well off for bone with strong rear quarters and a good level topline which he maintained on the move. 3 Harradine - Wildquest Samba Spirit of Halliana.

Junior ( 13 5 ) 1 Watkin's Wansleydale Rowanberry of Valsett eye catching orange youngster, compact and attractive in profile, pleasing head, excellent front and well set shoulders, forearms straight and widely sprung ribs, strong rear quarters, moved soundly. 2 Jolly's Wansleydale Loganberry at Jolymore - attractive blue, pleasing head and dark eye, good front, shoulders well set back, short and level back, well ribbed up, good rear quarters, stifles well bent, moved soundly. 3 Wansleydale Huckleberry at Steeplow.

Yearling ( 5 2 ) 1 Golby's Shadymoore Cowboys 'n' Kisses well constructed orange, very good bone and pleasing when viewed in profile, good head, nice reach of neck let into well set shoulders, level topline held well on the move, shown in good coat. 2 Wright's Fishwick Darling Lad very close to 1 and these two oranges could easily change places another day, pleasing head, clean muscular neck, good body properties, strong rear quarters, shown in good coat. 3 Andrews' Llinlow Impressionist.

Maiden ( 5 2 ) 1 Brown's Tattersett Double Barrel unplaced in a good Junior class but a worthy class winner here, nice shape of head in profile, good reach of neck let into well laid shoulders, level topline with tail correctly set almost in line with the back. 2 Taylor Atyeo's Pewterspeare Pirate Cove nicely shaped blue, good front and rear angulation shown in good coat, moved happily. 3 Shadwell's Swannery Dark Secret. Novice ( 5 3 ) 1 Wood's Bournehouse Lord Harry attractive blue, pleasing head and dark eye, very nice shape in outline, strong straight and rounded bone in forequarters, body properties good with widely sprung ribs, wide loins and strong hindquarters, moved soundly. 2 Brown's T D Barrel.

Tyro ( 5 3 ) 1 Lenzi's Pilsdon Jack-A-Dandy orange boy, good overall shape, excellent bone, correct shoulder placement, forearms straight, deep in back ribs, well muscled including strong second thighs, moved soundly. 2 Wood's B L Harry.

Graduate Dog ( 7 1 ) 1 Slack's Ravensett Dark Fire quite a dark blue well built dog, proud head and dark eye, good rounded bone, short pasterns, shoulders set back, well sprung ribs and deep in back ribs, strong muscular rear legs, good bend of stifles allowing the dog to move soundly. 2 Grimsdell's Tattersett Final Edition pleasing tri when seen in profile, good body properties with quality forequarters, well set shoulders, back short and level and well ribbed up, good rear angulation, shown in good coat. 3 Ball's Bondgate Wayward Lad From Beaverhill.

Post Graduate ( 7 1 ) 1 Tucker's Walshaw Moonstorm attractive blue, most pleasing of heads, dark eye and appealing expression, nice shape in profile, good forequarters with correct shoulder placement and well defined hindquarters, stifles well let down, moved soundly, just needs a little more time to reach full maturity. 2 Critchell-Imms' Tattersett Smoke Screen a well made tri, pleasing in head and expression, well rounded bone, shoulders well set back, deep chest and good spring of rib, well presented and moved well. 3 Kirsch's Soul Mate of Sorbus.

Limit ( 11 3 ) 1 Wells' Hollygrove Story Teller At Ritanor attractive blue with the most appealing of heads so well proportioned, expressive dark eyes which complete the picture, very good shape in outline and does not disappoint on examination, good bone, sound forequarters, lean slightly arched neck let into well set back shoulders, body well ribbed up, hindquarters strong and muscular, well coated and moved with style covering the ring effortlessly. Pleased to award him the CC and to have the Referee award him B.O B. 2 Day's Decoverly Celtic Venture a very good compact tri dog pleasing overall shape, attractive head, good dark eye and expression, well placed shoulders, strong body properties and sound rear quarters enabling him to move well with a good driving ation off the hocks. Pleased to award him the R.C.C. 3 Mellish's Harvancourt In Touch With Monbrec.

Open ( 12 4 ) 1 Hill & Littlechild's Sh Ch Ravensett American Gigalo At Somerled dark blue, lovely shape in outline, well proportioned head and good dark eye, strong forquarters, correct shoulder placement, level topline, good bend of stifle, well presented in good coat, lost to the CC winner in the challenge on movement. 2 Derry's Sh Ch Balvenie What A Sensation orange with a pleasing head and expression, well constructed both front and and quarters, good shoulders and top line, not in the best of coats on the day and movement whilst sound lacked his usual sparkle. 3 Andrews' Llinlow Sovereign Gold.

Special Beginners ( 6 1 ) 1 Slack's Ravenset D Fire. 2 Stephenson's Wansleydale H A Steeplow placed third in a strong Junior class - a well made tri, pleasing shape in profile both standing and on the move, straight in front, good shoulder placement, lean muscular neck, strong hindquarters, shown in good coat and moved soundly. 3 Jolley's Dyrham Dont Stop Me Now In Jolymore.
Elwyn Evans
Judge
21st November, 2007.

DOGS

MPD: Ball & Morgans GEMSETT I AM LEGEND. At just 7mths this young blue dog is very well balanced, with a lovely head and eye excellent neck and shoulders good front. Correct angulation deep chest and when settled true on the move.

PD:7(1) 1st. Grimsdells TATTERSETT DOCTOR WOODY. Loved this 10 month old blue boy, best of heads with kind eye, scores in neck and shoulder placement, great forechest, excellent body proportions, deep chest strong quarters moves straight and true coming and going. In full puppy coat BPD. 2nd Woods SWANNERY MAGICAL MOMENT. Everything to like about this puppy, lovely make and shape just needs time to mature. 3rd Harradines MANDYSET POP IDOL AT HALLIANA

VD 6(1). 1st. Jolleys BELLESETT MASTERPIECE OF JOLYMORE. 10 year old orange who moved free and true with a good head and expression. Good depth, straight front and strong rear, kept his topline on the move. 2nd. Mellishs OWNWAYS MOVING SHADOW FOR MONBREC.Blue, well constructed, pleasing head and expression in excellent coat not quite as true as 1 on the move today.3rd. Marshalls RIGHT SED FRED AT CHEYNEYGATE

JD 4(2). 1st. Loakes GOLDBIRCH GUYS N DOLLS. Orange who at 14 months is just starting to mature. Beautiful head and expression with dark kind eyes, good front legs and feet, scores in neck into level topline with deep chest and correct angulated quarters strong sound free movement, a bright future I would hope. 2nd. Darleys SEVENSETT MASK OF ZORRO. Lovely headed dog, dark eye good body proportions well angulated but not as together as 1

YD 2. 1st. Fishers BEECHANGER WAGTAIL. Orange 19months old with pleasing head, good neck, shoulders and topline deep chest straight front well angulated throughout sound mover .2nd. Devilles SWANNERY MAGIC LEGEND. Orange heavier build than 1 but balanced nevertheless masculine head with kind eye, deep chest, strong rear movement, preferred front of 1
MD 2(1wd). 1st. Grimsdells TATTERSETT DOCTOR WOODY.
ND 3(1). 1st. Loakes GOLDBIRCH GUYS N DOLLS. 2nd. Grimsdells TATTERSETT DOCTOR WOODY

TD 3. 1st. Loakes GOLDBIRCH GUYS N DOLLS. 2nd. Lenzis PILSDON JACK A DANDY. Orange who has all the essentials, Good head, soft expression, good hind quarters, balanced outline just needs coat to finish the picture. 3rd. Andrews LINLOW IMPRESSIONIST

GD 5. 1st. Hepburns TATTERSETT DOUBLE STRAND. Tri with pleasing head, good neck shoulders and outline,well balanced, deep chest, moved well with strong quarters in full coat. 2nd. Browns TATTERSETT DOUBLE BARRELL. Litter brother to 1 same remarks apply but did not have the full coat of his brother .3rd. Critchell-Imms BARTHOLEYS BOGART

PGD 10(1). 1st. Wrights FISHWICK DANCING LAD. Orange of substance super clean outline, lovely refined head with soft expression, good layback of shoulder & upper arm, tight feet, deep chest , good spring of rib, strong quarters, in good coat moved true when settled. 2nd. Wellers BOURNEHOUSE INSIGNIA AT JULDEANE.Orange in full coat and well balanced. Good head and expression, balanced outline, well angulated, kept his topline on the move, wasn't quite as settled as one. 3rd. Grimsdells TATTERSETT FINAL EDITION

LD 11(2). 1st. Stubbington & Buckleys BONDGATE SINGLE MALT. Super Orange dog who today was the star for me. Commanded attention straight away. Lovely upstanding masculine dog from any angle looked a picture standing and did not disappoint when gone over. Beautiful head and expression with flowing neck into well laid shoulders and upper arm. Excellent topline held on the move, deep chest, strong loin, straight front excellent feet. In full flowing coat which was put down to perfection, well deserved his 3rd CC and subsequently BIS. 2nd. Tuckers WALSHAW MOONSTORM. Handsome blue dog, slightly smaller than 1 but very well balanced with a super head and expression clean through neck, shoulders and upper arm, good topline ,strong loin, well presented and in good condition. 3rd. Days DECOVERLEY CELTIC VENTURE

OD 8 (1). 1st. Dennis SH CH MARIGLEN PENTGSSONS LEGACY. Well known champion who still is one of my favourites, has everything, beautifully made, lovely head and expression, good neck and shoulder placement, super forehand , straight front , deep chest strong quarters producing good movement, today the limit winner had the edge, but thoroughly deserved the RCC. 2nd. Hepburns JULDEANE PRINCE OF BLUES. Balanced blue with a pleasing outline. Correct head and dark eye with soft expression , good lay of shoulder and upper arm strong quarters moved with drive keeping his topline in full coat. 3rd. Youngs OWNWAYS MONEY TALKS
SBD 7 . 1st. Loakes GOLDBIRCH GUYS N DOLLS. 2nd. Hepburns TATTERSETT DOUBLE STRAND. 3rd. Shadwells SWANNERY DARK SECRET
Linda Cooper
Judge
SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER CHAMPIONSHIP SHOW
Sunday 23 November 2008 at Tidworth Leisure Centre

MINOR PUPPY, BITCH 2(1) . 1st LEWIS Mr K.E. & Mrs G.M. KEGIL GOLDEN DELICIOUS Just six months old, well balanced baby, sweet head and expression, dark eye, correct mouth, in lovely condition, moved very soundly for her age. Very promising puppy.

PUPPY, BITCH 6 . 1stBAKER Mrs G. MANDYSET POP TART. 10mth old dark tri, full of energy, lovely head and expression, good shoulders, top line and hind quarters, never stopped wagging her tail showing true setter spirit. Very pleased she was awarded best puppy in show. 2nd PITTS Mr S. WANDSFELL TISWAS. Another quality puppy, not quite as forward as 1, but nevertheless deserving her 2nd place. Stricking colour, very sound, will watch her progress.

VETERAN, BITCH 6(3) 1ST. TUCKER Mrs C. J. WALSHAW LET'S PARTY. Very nice class of oldies but at 9yrs old this was my winner. Still moving well and holding her outline, lovely coat and condition. Best veteran in show. 2nd DUNKS Mr & Mrs P. J. SAMELEN STAR BRIGHT. A favourite of mine, lovely bitch, also very fit and enjoying her day, but not quite the verve of 1.
J UNIOR, BITCH 4(3). 1ST BAKER Mrs G. MANDYSET WANNA BE A ROCK STAR. Although alone, deserving of a 1st. Very excitable, but well made and balanced.

YEARLING, BITCH 8(6). 1ST LITTLECHILD Mrs S. & DAVIES Mrs RAVENSETT DARK SECRETS. Blue bitch, excelled in neck and shoulders, lovely straight top line and hind quarters, moved very well with lovely tail action. 2nd DAVIS Mrs Y. CULVERWELL CALYPSO OF MERLEYCOPSE Bigger type of bitch, carrying much more coat than 1 but a little overweight and loose in her movement.
MAIDEN, BITCH 3(2) . 1ST NEATH Mrs J. ALBADORA MISS QUIZADORA Placed vhc in puppy, very raw, moved much better in this class but needs time.
NOVICE, BITCH 5(4) . 1ST BAKER Mrs G. MANDYSET WANNA BE A ROCK STAR. 1ST in Junior Bitch
TYRO, BITCH 2(2).

GRADUATE, BITCH 3 1ST . DAY Mrs J. DECOVERLY MAMMA MIA. Very nice orange bitch, lovely expression and good mouth, very short coupled straight front and short hocks. Lovely mover. 2nd HEWITT Mr & Mrs D. TATTERSETT DOUBLE ACTION Another well made bitch, very feminine, moved well, not quite the coat and condition of 1.

POST GRADUATE, BITCH 7(2) . 1ST HARRIS Ms. L. Harris & DENISS Mrs J. BONDGATE EVENING STAR OVERMARIGLEN JW. Clearly the winner, this exquisite very well balanced tri bitch, with no exaggeration. Beautiful head, dark eye and the sort of soft expression I was looking for. Strong neck with good lay of shoulder. Straight front, good bend of stifle, lovely bone and well muscled, good depth and spring of rib. In the best of coats and condition, moved soundly and was thrilled to give her the CC. 2nd MARSHALL Miss D. A. CHEYNEYGATE BLESMA SOUL. Another sound bitch, finer than 1, not quite in the same coat and condition.

LIMIT, BITCH 12(2). 1ST GRIMSDELL Mr & Mrs A. TATTERSETT AIR OF ELEGANCE. Very feminine orange bitch, lovely head with dark eye and correct mouth. Looked a picture standing, she was also well muscled up which showed in her flowing movement. Unfortunately a little short of coat today and therefore reserve CC. 2nd DAY Mrs J. MANDYSET READY STEADY GO TO DECOVERLY. Another very nice bitch, a shade smaller in frame than 1. Well made, unfortunately really excitable which there her movement slightly.

OPEN, BITCH 11(3) 1ST LITTLECHILD Mrs S. SH. CH. RAVENSETT BIANCA. Very elegant feminine bitch. Lovely straight front, level top line, presented and showed extremely well, unfortunately also short of coat. 2nd MONTELL Mrs A. CULVERWELL SUMMER COLOURS. Tri bitch, slightly heavier type but well made, plenty of bone, in good coat and condition, moved extremely well.

SPECIAL BEGINNERS, BITCH 4(2) . 1ST DAVIS Mrs Y. CULVERWELL CALYPSO OF MERLEYCOPSE. 2ND in Yearling. 2nd .GREENHAM Mr & Mrs T A Greenham LEWKINS WIDELOAD WINNIE AT FRIZZANTI. Orange bitch, dark eye, level topline, good bend of stifle and sound mover.
