pages.title: open show critique 2010
blocks: SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY OPEN SHOW 18.7.10.

What a lovely way to spend a Sunday ... judging a breed show on a typical English village green in glorious sunshine and a slight breeze. This proved something of a walkover for the fairer sex with bitches taking all the major awards. Whilst my winners impressed me, I found the most common faults to be lack of angulation front and back with the corresponding restricted profile movement. I was also surprised to see so much untidy dentition in such a moderate gundog breed. The exhibitors were extremely sporting.

MPD (1) 1. Jones’ Kerrimere Catch a Dream for Redbornstoke, 6 ½ months orange of quality, masculine head with kind expression. At the moment at the rather “bum high” stage, needing to drop into his rear and feet need to tighten. Basically good balance and angulation throughout and he is already well ribbed. Moves with some scope in profile but needs to tighten coming and going.

PD (4) 1. Rush’s Tattersett Future Gamble, 11 months orange of excellent overall type and shape. His head needs to break as at the moment he appears a little shallow in stop, but it is well balanced and his expression pleases. Excellent bone and rib with good feet and he has optimum angulation. Despite his age he moved really well, up, down and around. BPIS to his litter sister who at the moment appeals more in head. Should finish up really well and I am sure has a great future. 2. K. Catch a Dream for R. 3. Stephenson’s Wistaston Starting School at Steeplow.

VD (2) 1. Tompsett’s Radbrooks Break Away, 9 year old blue of good overall type and balance. Masculine head but a shade lippy, excellent bone and feet, good angulation front and back, well ribbed and holds his topline well. Moved steadily. BV. 2. Sayers’ Mariglen Take Me I’m Yours for Christter, 7 ½, heavily boned and strong headed, good basic type, not as true moving as 1 and tends to break in topline.

JD (4) 1. Thompson’s Ravensett Ralph Lauren, blue just out of Puppy and whilst not a sudden-impact kind of dog on the stack, when he moves he pulls himself together and coordinates beautifully. Lovely quality head, good bone and feet but with maturity he should develop in forechest and this causes him to stand a little ten-to-two in front. Perfectly balanced outline, just a little light in body condition which is probably just an age thing. Looks his best when moving as he uses his angulation so well, covering the ground freely and with great ease. Could develop into something special. 2. Watkins & Hayden’s Mariglen Snowdrift at Hayworth, 17 months blue who set up looked the obvious winner. Lots of type and shape about him and he is better bodied than 1 with good bone but could have tighter feet. Pleasing head and expression, well balanced throughout. Moves true up and down but in profile tends to snatch in front. 3. Hill’s Mandyset Slippery Customer.
YD (1) 1. M. Snowdrift at H.

ND (1) 1. Salmon’s Burleycott Irish Cream, 2 year old orange, all male to the point of being a little strong in backskull. Well boned and ribbed, stands a little untidily in front and topline tends to be a little high at the rear. Moved quite steadily.

GD (1) 1. Wood’s Swannery Magical Moment, 2 year old blue, unexaggerated and typy, good basic head proportions but a little skully. Excellent bone and feet, well ribbed, ideal angulation with well balanced outline. Comes on true but goes away a little close and could have more rear drive.

PGD (4) 1. Loakes’ Goldbirch Guys n Dolls, 2 year old orange who proved one of the most frustrating dogs of the day. He has such a lovely way of going, having great style and ring presence and he moves on a loose lead with ease and power, but when he sets up he tends to stiffen and lose his rear angulation. Excellent head and expression, well ribbed, firm topline and ideal balance of outline. Had I judged purely on the move he way well have gone one better; as it was, he ended up RBD. When taking photographs later I made a few handling suggestions to his owner and we managed to set him up where he made the best of his rear angulation. With some work I feel he is good enough to make up. 2. Sketchley’s Kerrimere Royal Design, 3 years old orange who on the stack looked the probable winner as he clearly has greater length from hip to hock than 1 and more turn of stifle. Glorious head and expression, well boned with tight feet and well sprung ribs. Really liked him but sadly on the move he was rather lethargic and could not match 1 going away or around. 3. Taylor & Atyeo’s Pewterspeare Pirate Cove.

LD (4) 1. Dunks’ Samelen One Man, 4 ½ years orange with a beautiful head and soft expression. Makes a pleasing overall picture when set up but a little more angulation front and back would enable him to open up a little more on the go-around. 2. Kirsch’s Soul Mate of Sorbus, 6 years blue of excellent type and shape and I see litter brother to BD so it is no surprise that he is the same overall stamp. Well balanced head, clean flowing outline, just a little sluggish compared to 1 and rather blousy coming on. 3. Taylor & Atyeo’s Harvancourt Nice Touch.

OD (2) 1. Kirsch’s Shining Star of Sorbus. 6 years blue of excellent overall type and balance. Well balanced masculine head which could perhaps have a little more work in it, strong but clean neck, moderately angulated front and back with good forechest and well sprung ribs. Moves steadily and soundly if not with the greatest enthusiasm but I felt his overall correctness merited BOS. 2. Hammond’s Hartsett Going for Gold with Oaktrish, 4 years orange with lovely head and expression and good basic shape. Not as well filled in front as 1 and his movement is not his strongest feature.
SBD (3) 1. S. Magical Moment. 2. B. Irish Cream. 3. Pead’s Sparsett Hembury Explorer of Lakeview.

MPB (2) 1. Tompsett’s Radbrooks Kokomo, 6 months heavily marked blue with some promise. Feminine head, obviously at this age she needs to drop into her rear but she has excellent basic conformation which manifests itself when she opens up so impressively on the move. Already happy and confident, should do well with full maturity. 2. Sketchley’s Kerrimere Lindy Lou, 6 months orange with a glorious head and expression who needs to gain confidence and use her tail. Well boned and ribbed, feet a little open and she could have a little more neck to balance. Rather choppy mover.

PB (3) 1. Brown’s Tattersett Flutter Money, really classy 11 months orange who made a great impression. Beautiful head and expression, elegant neck, optimum angles front and back with already good bone and rib. Beautifully conditioned, just needs to drop into her rear with maturity but she is already a very impressive mover, going accurately up and down and covering the ground easily in profile. Should have a glittering future and also has the advantage of a very capable handler. BPIS. 2. Pitts’ Wandsfell Just Love Me, 9 months more heavily marked orange. Quality feminine head, good bone but feet not as neat as 1. Stacked throws out an impressive outline with excellent angulation. Goes around well but needs to tighten considerably in front. 3. Osborne’s Llinlow Caribbean Night.

JB (3) 1. Grimsdell’s Tattersett Hebe at first glance this 18 months tricolour bitch leapt out at me for her perfect balance and complete lack of exaggeration. On the first go-around she thrilled me even more as she has such flawless footfall, great scope and lightness of foot. Although she was a little skittish when I first handled her back end, getting hands on her was a joy as everything fits and flows and she is the kind of dog that reminds us judges of the importance of moderation. Beautiful head with ideal planes and kind expression, elegant but strong neck, already well filled forechest and sprung ribs, firm hard backline and correctly set and carried tail. At this age she is not dripping in coat but this merely emphasised her classic lines and overall correctness. Should sail through to her title. I loved her! BIS. 2. Day’s Mandyset Rumour Has It, 13 months orange with a beautiful head and expression. Feet not as neat as 1 and she doesn’t have her rear angulation. Excellent neck and shoulder but needs to tighten moving up and down. 3. Stirk & Littlechild’s Ravensett Royal Diamond for Drakar.

YB (1) 1. Lewis’ Sunrush Silvery Moon, 23 months blue with basically good head type if a shade lippy. Pleasing basic shape, good bone and rib and her outline and angles please on the stack. Could move with more determination and strengthen behind.

NB (3) 1. T. Flutter Money. 2. Evans & Paterson’s Manorroy Mandarin Lady, nearly 3 years orange of excellent type. Lovely head and eye and constructionally she is so good to go over, being well put together, correctly angulated and well ribbed and boned. A very correct bitch all through who moved so soundly ... I just wish she appeared to enjoy herself more! I gather this was only her second show so maybe she will soon decide that it’s not such an ordeal and then could so some interesting winning. 3. Aldridge’s Ravensett Diamond Lil at Fleckers.
GB (2) 1. M . Mandarin Lady. 2. R. Diamond Lil at F., 2 years blue with a classy head and balanced outline who looked a picture standing. Sadly she constantly paced and moved very stiffly behind.

PGB (2) 1. Stirk’s Ravensett Diamond Romance with Grakar, 2 years tricolour beautifully presented and handled. Stacked she immediately draws the eye as she is perfectly balanced and everything fits and flows. Really good head profile but I felt she could have a little more finish of foreface when I got on top of her. Excellent neck, topline, angulation and she is well ribbed and boned. Makes a very striking overall picture standing and she moves true but did not have the exceptional frontal reach of the BIS winner. Even so well deserved RBB and later RBIS. 2. Hall’s Koolunga Silver Dawn, 4 years orange with an appealing head and eye, elegant neck, firm bone and well sprung rib. Not the rear angulation of 1, a little choppy in front movement and tends to break in topline on the go-around.

LB (1) 1. Grimsdell’s Tattersett Double Florin, 3 ½ years blue of excellent overall type and with a look of quality. Nicely balanced head if a shade light in eye. Could have a little more development of forechest for her age but she impresses in general outline when stacked with excellent angulation front and back. Could have been a little more fluid on the move.

OB (1) 1. Hall’s Tattersett Dreaming Away of Koolunga, 6 years orange of excellent overall type. Pleasing head with kind eye, well boned and ribbed, but could have a little more angulation at both ends. Moved adequately around but could have more rear drive and didn’t have the sparkle of the younger bitches.
SBB (2) 1. M. Mandarin Lady. 2. S. Silvery Moon.
ANDREW H. BRACE (Judge)

pages.title: open show critique 2010
blocks: SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY OPEN SHOW - Sunday 18th July 2010
Firstly I would like to thank the committee for making my day so enjoyable. It was a very pleasant and venue and everyone seemed friendly and relaxed.
MICHAEL WINCH YEARLING MEMORIAL AWARD (DOG OR BITCH)

7(1) 1. Pitts’s WANDSFELL JUST LOVE ME. Nine month old dark orange belton bitch in lovely coat and condition. Sweet head with lovely dark eye giving that soft expression. Arch neck leading into good lay-back of shoulder. Good bone with level topline and good bend of stifle. Moved well just needs to tighten in front movement.

2. Day’s MANDYSET RUMOUR HAS IT. Lighter orange bitch with lovely head and expression and dark eye. Excellent layback of shoulder, short coupled with good spring of rib. Movement rather erratic to start with but settled when moved again. 3. Grimsdell’s TATTERSETT HEBE.
LESLEY ALLEN-SCOTT OPEN MEMORIAL AWARD (DOG OR BICH)

16(5) 1. Sayers’s MARIGLEN BLUE FLAME FOR CHRISTER. What a star! In beautiful coat and condition. Lovely head and expression - just what I like in and English Setter. Good bone and feet, strong arched neck with well laidback shoulder. Level topline and good rear angulation. This dog has a lot of ring presence and moves well when settled. 2. Wright’s FISHWICK DANCING LAD. Another lovely dog but today did not show his best on the move. Nice head with dark eye, good bone with tight feet, excellent shoulder placement, good spring of rib and bend of stifle. In good coat and condition. When standing this dog has an elegant outline. Very sound mover. These two dogs could easily change places on another day. 3. Kirch’s SOUL MATE OF SORBUS
Judge Margaret Henry (Beechanger)

pages.title: open show critique 2011
blocks: SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY - OPEN SHOW - 17 July 2011

I would like to take this opportunity to thank the committee of the Southern English Setter Society for inviting me to judge their Open Show and for their kind hospitality, to the stewards, Chris and John for their able assistance in the ring, and to the exhibitors who gave me such a good entry with few absentees. Unfortunately the weather was not kind and the judging had to done inside the village hall.

I thoroughly enjoyed my day of judging and was not disappointed in the overall quality of the exhibits present both in dogs and bitches. I was pleased to award Mariglen Snowdrift At Hayworth, Best in Show, Harvancourt Loving Touch, Reserve Best in Show, and Best Puppy in Show to Mariglen Gift Wrapped, all displaying character and style that is typical of this breed.

1. Mottishaw's Upperwood Hooray Henry, 6 mth dark B/B baby with everything just as it should be at this age. Dark well shaped eyes, good length to neck, well angulated front and rear. Correct tail set which he used well on the move, would prefer tighter feet but no doubt this will come with age. Lots of potential, BPD.
2. Taylor & Atyeo's Hazeysunsett Vivaldi, another lovely baby, not so quite together as 1st and needing to grow into himself. He had the better feet of the two, but was moving close behind.

1. Tompsett's Radbrooks Homeward Bound, masculine headed B/B dog, slightly more throaty than I would like. Adequate length of neck leading into correct topline, well angulated fore and aft, excellent feet, but close behind on the move.
VD. (5) Enjoyed judging this class, all were deserving of a 1st but a decision had to be made.

1. Holland's Mandyset Dirty Dancing, 91/2 year old B/B with pleasing head and gentle expression in his eyes. Good length to neck, straight front with good depth of rib. Well placed shoulders, correct rear angulation and carried his tail well on the move, positive mover around the ring.
2. Hammond's Hartsett Paper Skye For Oaktrish, well constructed O/B of 81/2 years, with masculine head, clean neck, with well sprung ribs. Plenty of bone and correct feet. Another who moved out well.
3. Kirsch's Soul Mate Of Sorbus.
JD. (3). Class of promising teenagers.

1. Murray & Berry's Harvancourt's Miracle, a well proportioned young man with a melting expression. Very well constructed with a good reach of neck, correct lay of shoulder and upper arm, good turn of stifle. Free flowing movement but just needs to body up, short of coat but that only emphasised his correct construction. Son of my best bitch winner and a masculine version of her. RBD.

2. Shadwell's Canonsett Grin N' Bear It, Handsome headed dog with dark well shaped eyes, long neck leading into correct topline and balanced angulation. Good legs and feet, moved well, but slightly close behind, liked him a lot.
3. Jolley & Taylor's Wansleydale Tribute To Jolymore.

1. Stephenson's Wistaston Starting School At Steeplow, O/B dog with a well-developed head, clean neck and straight front. Well laid back shoulders and pleasing rear assembly. Moved soundly on good legs and feet, well muscled. He was the best mover in the class and considered him for higher honours.
2. Shadwell's Canonsett Grin N' Bear It.
3. Pitts Wandsfell Just In Time.

1. Thompson's Ravensett Ralph Lauren, 2 yr old B/B who moved the better of the two. Well shaped head with soft expression, long neck leading to well-shaped shoulders. Well-sprung rib cage, good rear angulation, sound in movement.
2. Hill's Mandyset Slippery Customer, O/B dog with a pleasing masculine head, but found him a little throaty for my taste. Nice balanced outline, but not moving out as well as winner.
GD. (6). Movement in this class was generally not so good.

1. Cook's Moorbrook Firecracker At Pernickety, O/B dog with a handsome masculine head but a touch throaty. Correct reach of neck, well laid shoulders, straight front and well angulated rear. Well developed body, good feet, well presented coat. Adequate mover.

2. Slack's Ravensett Renaissance, dark B/B dog, close decision between these two, just preferred the feet of the winner. Well constructed throughout with correct placed shoulders and well angulated rear. Just did not give of his best on the move.
3. Shadwell's Canonsett Grin N' Bear It.

1. Bridgewater, Davies & Jeffery's Brucelm Diamond Harry Rocks Bridgella, masculine dog with a well-shaped head and a glint in his eye. Well placed shoulders and upper arm, correct spring of rib, short coupled with plenty of bone. Good bend of stifle, level topline held on the move which he did with reach and drive. Well presented, loved this dog and his attitude to life, close to top honours, Rock on Harry!!
2. Wood's Swannery Magical Moment, appealing masculine head with a kind eye. Clean neck, level topline held on the move. Well angulated front and strong quarters, moved out well.
3. Oliver's Bramstorm Walk The Line.

1. Watkin's Mariglen Snowdrift At Hayworth, B/B/T dog of 21/2 years in immaculate coat, beautiful masculine head with soft expression in well shaped eyes. Elegant reach of neck flowing into good shoulder placement with good return of upper arm. Correct straight front, firm topline, short coupled body with well sprung ribs and strong through the loin. Powerful well-angulated hindquarters with well let down hocks, which he used to cover a lot of ground on the move with good tail action. An eye catching, all quality dog combining masculinity and the elegance that I was looking for, presented to perfection. BD & BIS.

2. Jolley's Wansleydale Loganberry At Jolymore ShCM, handsome 5 yr old B/B dog with lovely dark expressive eyes. Good reach of neck set on to good lay of shoulder with strong hindquarters. Has a nice profile, sound in movement, just not the pazzazz of the winner.
3. Morgan & Shadwell's Quensha Pinball Wizard.

1. Loakes Sh. Ch. Goldbirch Guys N Dolls JW Sh.CM, mature O/B dog with lovely head and correct shaped dark eye. Adequate neck and well balanced overall with straight front and well boned legs and correct shaped feet. Good depth of rib, strong hindquarters and well muscled. Moved well, but preferred the elegance of the limit winner in the challenge.
2. Hammond's Hartsett Going For Gold With Oaktrish, O/B with well developed head and clean neck. Well made fore and rear quarters, great substance all through and good coat and condition, moved OK.
3. Dunk's Samelen One Man.
SBD. (5)
1. Cook's Moorbrook Firecracker At Pernickety.
2. Shadwell's Canonsett Grin N' Bear It.
3. Wood's Swannery Magical Moment.
MP. (5,1). Loved all 4 babies in this class and I am sure that all will do well in the future.

1. Harris & Dennis's Mariglen Gift Wrapped, 7 month old B/B/T baby with the sweetest of heads, complete with lovely dark eye with a hint of naughtiness. Good reach of neck set into well-placed shoulders, correct length of body leading into well-angulated hindquarters. Moved out soundly with plenty of attitude and a waggy tail. when standing, showed a pleasing outline. BPB & BPIS.

2. Evans & Paterson,s Gillancette Emerald Lady, 6 month old O/B girl. Loved this one and at first glance I thought that this would be my winner, but not quite so together on the move as 1st. Beautiful well-shaped feminine head and eye, long neck and correct shoulder placement and good upper arm. Well-ribbed for age, level topline with correct tail carriage and well-angulated rear.
3. Tucker & Reith's Walshaw Snow Flurry.

1. Swannell's Rickory Buzy Lizzie, striking B/B/T youngster with gorgeous head. Long lean neck, well angulated front and rear giving a nicely balanced profile, well off for bone with excellent feet. On the move she persisted in throwing out her left hock which cost her BPB.

1. Dennis's Sh. Ch. Mariglen Flaming Colours, loved this elegant O/B, most feminine of heads with soft expressive eyes. Lovely over the neck and shoulders which are well laid back. A deep well-ribbed body, short coupled, with good turn of stifle. Tail well set on and used when on the move. Presented in excellent coat and condition. A sound positive mover. BVIS.

2. Aldridge's Salisbury Plain Babe At Fleckers, well constructed O/B with lovely head and expression. Clean neck, correct angulated shoulders, with good quarters and correct feet. Moved well enjoying her day out.
3. Davis's Merleycopse Love Of A Lady.

1. Deering's Rosetimber Foxy Breeze, young balanced B/B bitch of good size and type. Pleasing head and expression, correct reach of neck and lay of shoulder. Strong rear with good bend of stifle, firm topline held on the move and correct tail action. Well handled and presented.
2. Dennis's Mariglen Beautiful Dawn, promising O/B bitch with a long elegant neck and lay of shoulder. Good angulation behind with good length and depth of body.
3. Sharples' Mariglen Flaming Sunset.

1. Topsett's Radbrooks Kokomo, ultra feminine dark B/B with soft gentle expression. Good length of neck, well laid shoulders and good rear angulation with good feet. Held her topline on the move. A nicely balanced bitch, liked her a lot.
Sharples' Mariglen Flaming Sunset, a pretty, well proportioned bitch, clean neck merging into good shoulders. Straight forelegs and pleasing rear assembly. Presented in good condition.

1. Tucker's Walshaw Moonlight And Roses, pleasing B/B with lovely dark eye and expression. Good neck and shoulder placement. Well developed quarters, neat feet and correct tailset. Held her topline on the move, best mover in the class.

2. Cozen's Mandyset Blue Murder At Earldoms, very pretty B/B with good eye colour and shape. Good length to neck leading into clean shoulders, nicely angled with corresponding rear. Presented in good order but not putting all in on the move.
3. Aldridge's Ravensett Diamond Lil At Fleckers.

1. Sharples & Dennis's Mariglen Crystal Gayle, I have judged this attractive bitch before and my opinion of her has not changed. Sweetest of heads with well shaped eyes, long neck and good layback of shoulders. Correct length of upper arm, good length and depth of body with well sprung ribs. Strong well- muscled hindquarters. Overall outline very pleasing, moved well and true keeping her topline on the move. Shown in good coat and condition. Full of quality, just pipped by open winner on maturity hence RBB.

2. Oliver's Bramstorm Line Dancer, typical head and expression, correct angulation front and rear. Moved well using her tail to advantage. Close between these two, just preferred outline of the winner.
3. Cook's Moorbrook Uptown Flirt At Pernickety.

1. Reith's OwnwaysTouch N Tell, Lovely honest B/B bitch, presenting a good outline when stood. Sufficient length of neck, good front and well angulated rear used to advantage on the move. Good firm body condition.

2. Davis's Culverwell Calypso Of Merleycopse, O/B bitch with a pleasing head and kindly eye, good length of neck and level topline. Well constructed throughout, with very good feet, but unfortunately insisted on crabbing on the move.

1. Murray & Berry's Harvancourt Loving Touch, an elegant B/B with an exquisite head which took my eye as she entered the ring. Stunningly beautiful bitch with chiselled head and soft dark eyes and low set ears. Good long reachy neck, well angulated shoulders and good length of upper arm . Good depth of brisket and spring of rib, strong hindquarters with well bent stifles and best of feet. Sound on the move, outline shouts English Setter. BB & RBIS.

2. Deering's Rosetimber Foxy Lady, sweet headed B/B with elegant reach of neck, correct shoulder placement and straight front. Well sprung rib cage, Strong rear with correct angulation, firm topline held on the move, moved soundly around the ring.

1. Aldridge's Ravensett Diamond Lil At Fleckers, very pretty B/B with sweet eye and expression. Well set ears, long reach of neck and good topline, correct front and rear angulation. Well presented and handled, but did not give of her best when moving.
Brace. (2,1)
1. Kirsch's brace, well matched pair of B/B brothers moving in unison around the ring.
Judge: - Karen Stirk

pages.title: open show critique 2013
blocks: Southern English Setter Society Open Show 13th July 2013 at Chieveley Village Hall
Thank you for such a lovely entry, although there were a number of absentees some no doubt due to the very hot weather conditions. As always a very friendly and well run show.

MPD (3) 1 Hodge's Lakecastle Tomo O/B Well grown minor puppy, good head, low set ears, long neck into well laid shoulders, well bodied, level topline, good bend of stifle, neat feet moved well for one so young; 2 William's & Ralfe's Sorbus Pierre Cardin Mature in good coat for age good bone, level topline well bodied good spring of ribs, super bend of stifle, just a little proud of tail on the move but moved okay; 3 Feerick's Canonsett Highland Mist.

PD (2) 1 Sykes Daraquist Barry A Reef B/B Good head with low set ears, long arched neck into correct shoulders, level topline, well bodied, good deep body, short coupled, good bend stifle, neat feet, moved well, am sure he will continue his winning ways BPD; 2 Bryant & Hollis' Phenset Blue Max, well grown, liked his head, long neck just not the lay of shoulder of 1, level topline well angulated stifle good feet.

VD (5, 4) 1 Dunks Samelen One Man, remember this one as a puppy and he has grown into a worthy winner of this class although on his own on the day deserved his red card well made head, low set ears long arched neck into oblique shoulders good deep body well sprung ribs good bone level topline & tail set, moderate stifle, moved with drive a pleasure to watch. BVIS.

JD (4)1 Croft & Littlechild's Ravensett Royal Legacy with Thistlesett B/B Good head, lots of work good low ears, good neck into correct shoulders, level topline super tail set, neat feet, good spring of rib plenty of bone moved well and was more mature than 2; 2 Fisher's Beechanger dusty Miller O/B good head, low ears, long neck into good shoulders, level topline good bend of stifle, good feet; 3 Mellish's Gemsett Pole Position for Monbrec.

YD (4) 1 Seaman & Dennis' Mariglen Royal Flame O/B Good head plenty of work correct eyes, ears good, long neck into oblique shoulders, deep body and well sprung ribs, level topline and tail coming off the back short coupled, good bend of stifle, neat feet moved well in good condition; 2 Radbrooks god Only Knows Not as mature as 1 Good ear set & feet moved okay; Mellish's Mandyset Don't Stop Me Now with Monbrec.
ND (7, 1) 1 Ravensett Royal Legacy with Thistlesett; 2 Mariglen Royal Flame; 3 Phenset Blue Max.

GD (7, 2) 1 Pead's Sparsett Hembury Explorer of Lakeview Tri Well balanced, head okay, good earset, shoulders okay, in good coat, level back good bend of stifle well off for bone, moved well; 2 Birch & West's Hitides Gingerbread Man O/B loved his head, long neck and good shoulders, well bodied and ribbed, level topline, would have liked a little more behind; 3 Mellish's Gemsett Pole Position for Monbrec.
PG (3, 2) 1 Atyeo's Hazeysunsett Vivaldi B/B Super masculine head, lowset ears long neck into good shoulders, deep in body, good feet, moved well.

LD ((3, 1) 1Thompson's Ravensett Ralph Lauren B/B Super head, low ears head in proportion good earset, long neck into good shoulder placement, level back, well bodied, deep ribs and level topline, good bone, neat feet, moved well and in good coat, RBD; 2 Mellish's Walshaw Christmas Spirit at Monbrec head balanced with lots of work, good earset, long neck, well off for bone, level topline good tailset good bend of stifle, moved well, unlucky to meet 1 on the day.

OD (3, 1) 1Harradine's Mandyset Pop Idol at Halliana, O/B An impressive dog in great coat, first class condition & balanced, Good dark pigment balanced head very lowset ears long neck into correct shoulders, level topline, deep body, short coupled, well sprung ribs well bent stifle neat feet, moved with drive BD & RBIS; 2 Oliver's Bramstorm Walk The Line Tri, mature dog, well made head, long neck, short coupled, well bent stifle, good feet, moved well, unlucky to meet 1 today.
SB (3) 1 Sparsett Hembury Explorer or Lakeview; 2 Walshaw Christmas Spirit at Monbrec; 3 Culverwell Causing Chaos.

MPB (4, 2) 1Sharples Kanietter Silver Belles B/B just 7 mths Feminine head lowset ears long arched neck into oblique shoulders, short coupled deep body, good stifle moved well; 2 Henderson's Twyline Turbo Skyrocket O/B Sweetest of heads good pigment low ears good neck and shoulders, level topline well covered body could swop places on another day.

PB (3) Dennis' Mariglen Xanthe O/B Super young lady, feminine head, dark pigment, long neck into oblique shoulders level topline good bend of stifle, neat feet deep body and well off for coat moved well BPB & BPIS; 2 Sykes' Daraquist Abbi Riginal another super young lady dark pigment, low ears long neck level topline good deep in body; 3 Bryant & Hollis' Phenset Ruby Tuesday.

VB (5, 2) 1 Day's Mandyset Ready Steady Go to Decoverly O/B Almost 10 yrs feminine head dark pigment, long neck into correct shoulder placement, short coupled still held her topline and moved well; 2 Aldridge's Salisbury Plain Babe at Fleckers nearing 10 yrs good head, dark pigment low ears, short coupled well off for coat.

JB (7, 4) 1Harris' Gemsett Ultra Violet B/B Balanced head, correct eye and ear placement, long neck into correct shoulders, short level back into tail, good bend of stifle, neat feet, well balanced moved well; 2 Davis' Richecca Baby Doll of Merlycopse tri another super bitch good head, long neck into correct shoulders, well sprung ribs deep body, good stifle short coupled moved well; 3 Atyeo's Heolddu Precious Moment.
NB (5, 1) 1Harris' Gemsett Ultra Violet; 2 Davis' Richecca Baby Doll of Merlycopse;
3 Bryant & Hollis' Phenset Ruby Tuesday.
GB (3, 2) 1 Tucker & Reith's Walshaw Snow Flurry O/B Good head, arched neck level topline, short coupled, good bend stifle, good bone and feet.

PGB (5, 3) 1 Sharples Mariglen Flaming Sunset O/B Good head, dark pigment, very lowset ears, long arched neck into correct shoulder placement, deep body, level topline, short coupled, great bend stifle and well off for muscle moved well; 2 Tompsett's Radbrooks Kokomo B/B feminine head well made and balanced, low ears, long neck, level topline, short coupled, moved well.

LB (5, 3) 1 Day's Mandyset Rumour Has It At Decoverly O/B Balanced head well chiselled very low ears dark pigment, long neck into oblique shoulders, short level back into correct tailset, good bone, deep body, good bend stifle and well muscled rear neat feet, moved with drive and purpose BB & BIS; 2 Cozen's Mandyset Blue Murder for Earldoms loved her chiselled head, low set ears, good length of neck leading into correct shoulder placement, level back and good depth of rib, good bend of stifle neat feet, was carrying too much weight which let her down on the move.

OB (6, 3) 1 Davis' Culverwell Calypso Of Merleycopse O/B Feminine head low earset, level topline, short coupled good bend of stifle & neat feet moved well; 2 Aldridge's Ravensett Diamond Lil At Fleckers good head, long neck level topline, well sprung ribs, neat feet, moved well; 3 Bryant & Hollis' Phenset Silver Moon.
Brace (1) 1Bryant & Hollis 'Brace A well matched pairing of Mother & Daughter and although the first time in this class did not let their handler down and moved really well together.
Vera Lyons
Judge
SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY - OPEN SHOW -13 July 2013
SPECIAL AWARD CLASSES
Thank you to all the exhibitors for a lovely entry and braving the sunshine on what was the hottest day of the year.
MICHAEL WINCH YEARLING MEMORIAL AWARD (12, 3)

1. Sykes's Daraquist Barry A Reef, quality B/B boy of 10 months who stood out in this strong class. Handsome masculine head with a dark well shaped eye, low set ears and soft melting expression. Good reach of neck leading into well-placed shoulders, level topline and good tailset. Excellent bone with straight front and tight round feet. Good depth of chest and spring of rib for age. He presented an elegant and balanced profile when stood and covered the ground with tail slashing from side to side as he moved around the ring, I loved him and would have gladly taken him home. 2, Fisher's Beechanger Dusty Miller, handsome 14 month old O/B dog with lots to like, presenting a pleasing picture in profile and was not disappointed when I went over him. Masculine head with soft expression, muscular neck into well laid shoulders, deep in brisket, balanced outline with good angulation fore and aft, moved okay but not as well as winner on the day.3. Harris's Gemsett Ultra Violet.
LESLEY ALLAN-SCOTT OPEN MEMORIAL AWARD (13 ,7)

1. Tompsett's Radbrooks Kokomo, dark B/B girl who I have judged previously and was pleased to go over her again as since her maternity duties has matured nicely. She is elegant in appearance and balanced throughout, she has the prettiest of heads with dark eye and soft feminine expression. Clean neck of good length set on good lay of shoulders, with level topline, good depth to chest and well angulated in front and rear. She moved effortlessly around the ring with good driving rear action using her tail correctly. She was easily the best mover in this class. 2. Thompson's Ravensett Ralph Lauren, young man who is so elegant but still masculine and appeals so much for breed type. Good balanced head with square muzzle and well defined stop. He is well constructed throughout with sound conformation and balanced outline. Shown in excellent coat and condition. He carried his tail well on the move but lost out to 1st place as he was suffering from the heat, but I like him a lot. 3. Bryant & Hollis's Phenset Silver Moon.
Miss Zoe Stirk (Grakar)

pages.title: open show critique 2014
blocks: Southern English Setter Society open show13th July 2014
Judge: Mrs Anne Derry (Balvenie)

A big thank you to officers and committee for the wonderful hospitality extended to me at this lovely breed club open show. I really enjoyed my day and thank exhibitors for their courtesy and sporting acceptance of my decisions.

Best in show was the bitch Culverwell Calamity Jane, Reserve Best in Show was the dog Bramstorm Walk the Line, Best Puppy in Show was the dog Mandysett Leave it to Lewis at Halliana and the Best Veteran was the dog Sh Ch Fishwick Dancing Lad
Mpd(0)
Pd (1)

1 Harradine's Mandysett Leave it to Lewis at Halliana . Nearly twelve month old tri dog, just right for his age. Clean outline, good reach of neck into well laid back shoulders. Masculine head, but not over done, low set ears and lovely dark eyes. Well off for bone, well ribbed up and plenty of body. Good rear angulation. When settled he moved well, using his tail and maintaining his top line. Feet just need to tighten. Best puppy dog and Best puppy in show
Vd (2)

1 Wright's Sh Ch Fishwick Dancing Lad, 8 year old darker orange presenting a balanced outline and in good coat and condition. Masculine head with dark eyes, reachy neck into good layback of shoulders. Short coupled and with good rear angulation. Strode out well, maintaining top line on the move. Enjoyed his day out and was happy to award him best veteran in show.

2 Dunks Samelen one Man, lighter orange of nearly 9years. Another with balanced outline, though slightly longer cast than 1. Masculine head and good reach of neck into well laid back shoulders. Not quite the rear angulation of the class winner. In good coat and condition. Moved with drive, but not just as true as 1 in front.
Class4 Junior dog (4 , 1 absent)

1 Mellish's Walshaw Blinded by Love for Monbrec, blue dog of 13months with lots to like. Smaller mould but still masculine. Correct head, with lovely dark eye and low set ears. Well laid back shoulders. Well off for bone and body, well ribbed up. Short coupled, with good rear angulation. Moved well, once he settled

2 Bennett's Mariglen Blue Star, 17 month old blue. Slightly longer cast and not quite as together as the winner. Masculine head, but just lacking in stop at the moment. Well laid back shoulders and OK for bone. Rear angulation not quite as good as 1, but did move with drive. Just needs time to come together.
3 Gilbert's Brucelm Wyke Hill of Shadowood
Yd (5, 2 absent)

1 Feerick's Canonsett Highland Mist, dark blue dog of 18 months. Masculine head, but not over done. Dark eye and correct ear set. Reachy neck into well laid back shoulders, short coupled. Good rear angulation, moved well once settled, maintained top line on the move. Not in his best coat yet, but this will complete the picture as he matures.

2 Kirsch's Sorbus Hugo Boss, light orange of 20 months. Masculine head and dark eye, correct ear set. Good reach of neck, but not the layback of shoulder of 1. Slightly longer cast, but still balanced. Good rear angulation and moved out well, just slightly proud of his tail at the moment.
3 Hodge's Lakecastle Tomo
Nd (4, 1 absent)
1 Mellish's Walshaw Blinded by love for Monbrec, 2 Frederick's Canonsett Highland Mist, 3 Kirsch's Sorbus Hugo Boss
GD (4)

1 Tompsett's Radbrooks God only knows, smaller made but really balanced blue dog. Masculine head with good stop, dark eye and correct ear set. Good reach of neck into well laid back shoulders. Well ribbed up and good angulation behind. Shown in super hard condition, moved well.

2 Leather's Meldor-sett Laird of Avalon at Pewterspeare (imp) dark tri dog of heavier build. Masculine head, good layback of shoulder and well ribbed up. Well off for bone and substance. Good rear angulation and moved with drive. Just not as true on the move as 1
3 Warrington's Culverwell Causing Chaos
Pgd

1 and reserve best dog Whittington's Juldeane Excalibur ShCM, one I have judged and liked before. Lovely balanced tri, with masculine head and dark eye. Good layback of shoulder and correct return of upper arm. Well off for bone and body. Good rear angulation, moved well and true coming and going. Shown in good coat and condition. Just lost out to open winner for best dog on maturity. His best is yet to come.

2 Croft and Littlechild's Ravensett Royal Legacy with Thistlesett, dark blue with lovely masculine head and dark eye. Reachy neck into well laid back shoulders,straight front. Well ribbed up and correct rear angulation. Not the drive of 1 on the move, nor as true. Shown in splendid coat.
3 Atyeo's Hazysunsett Vivaldi
Ld(2)
1 Wood's Swannery Magical Moment dark blue with masculine head and dark eye. Adequate reach of neck into good layback of shoulder. Shown in good coat. Good rear angulation and moved with drive

2 Harradine's Mandysett Matinee Idol at Halliana,orange dog with lovely outline. Masculine head with melting setter expression. Good reach of neck and well laid back shoulders. Well off for bone and body. Correct rear angulation and tail set. Thought he would be my class winner but he just did not get it together on the move. I am sure he will do well once his movement is sorted.
OD (2)

1and best dog Oliver's Bramstorm Walk the Line , dark tri dog with balanced outline. Masculine head and correct low ear set. Good layback of shoulder and return of upper arm. Well ribbed up and plenty of body and bone. Well angulated rear and correct tail set. Not in his best coat, but nothing to hide. Moved well and with drive. Reserve Best in Show

2Salmon's Burleycott Irish Cream, light orange with masculine head. Good layback of shoulder and well off for body and bone. Also not in his best coat. Moved true and with drive. His handler improves each time she shows.
Beginners dog (5)

1 Juldeane Excalibur, 2Culverwell causing chaos, tri dog with masculine head. Adequate reach of neck and layback of shoulder. Well bodied and well ribbed up. Good rear angulation. Moved well once he settled. 3 Burleycott Irish Cream
Mpb (2)

1and best puppy bitch Stirk's Mariglen Perfect Day for Grakar 8 month old blue bitch with lovely balanced outline. Sweetest of heads and lovely dark eye. Reachy neck and well laid back shoulders. Good body and bone. Straight front and good rear angulation. Very steady on the move and true coming and going. Reserve best puppy in show, just losing out to the dog on maturity.

2 Oliver's Wansleydale Fairie Queen at Bramstorm Similar comments as for class winner. Pretty orange bitch, who really played her handler up today. Not quite the balance of 1 at the moment and not as steady, or true on the move
Two very promising puppies
Pb
1 Wansleydale Fairie Queen at Bramstorm

2 Longstaff and Waller's Mandyset May Contain Nuts, blue bitch of 11 months. Lacking in maturity at the moment and unsettled when being gone over. Pretty girl, with reasonable angulation front and rear. Needs to body up. Moved true. Just needs time.
Vb (2)

1 Rockall's Settrenda Golden Fern at Lesnee, dark orange bitch of 7 years. Feminine head and dark eye. Good reach of neck into well laid back shoulders. Tight front and well ribbed up. Good rear angulation. Moved true, driving out well. Obviously enjoyed her day out. Reserve best veteran in show

2 Davis's Culverwell Calypso of Merlycopse, 7 and a half lighter orange. Feminine head and reachy neck. Not the layback of shoulder of 1. Well bodied, but longer cast than class winner. Moved with drive, just not as true as 1. Good coat and condition, a credit to her owner.
Jb(2 1 absent)

1 and best bitch and Best in Show Montell's Culverwell Calamity Jane, light tri bitch of 16 months. Lovely feminine head and dark eye, correct ear set. Straight front, reachy neck into excellent shoulders. Well off for bone and body. Well ribbed up and good rear angulation. Presented a super balanced outline and moved with drive, maintaining top line. In gleaming coat and condition. Alone in the class but a very worthy winner who filled my eye. Very happy to award her Best in Show
Yb (3 1 absent)

1 Rockall's Settrenda Promise of Love for Lesnee, feminine tri bitch. Lovely head with dark eye and correct ear set. Good reach of neck into well angulated shoulders. Well off for bone and well ribbed up. Good rear angulation used to effect on the move. True coming and going. Shown in good coat.
2 Mandyset May Contain Nuts
Nb (4 1 absent)
1 Mariglen Perfect Day for Grakar

2 Collis and Passey's Richecca Fallen Angel, pretty light orange with good reach of neck, but not the layback of shoulder of 1. Well bodied and good rear angulation. Moved true but not as steadily as the winner. Shown in good conditio
3 Settrenda Promise of Love for Lesnee
Gb (6. 2absent)

1 Cooper's Settrenda Promise to Love, feminine orange bitch with sweet head. Good reach of neck and well laid back shoulders. Plenty of body and well ribbed up. Lovely neat feet and moved well once settled. Shown in good coat and condition

2 Davis's Richecca Baby Doll of Merlycopse , tri bitch of larger build than 1. Balanced head and lovely dark eye, adequate reach of neck and good layback of shoulder. Correct rear angulation and moved out well, just not as true as class winner. Shown in lovely coat.
3 Stirk's Twyline Truly Skysablaze over Grakar
Pgb (3)

1 Atyeo's Hazysunsett Carisimi pretty blue bitch with feminine head. Reachy neck and correct front. Good shoulder angulation. Well ribbed up and plenty of bone and body. Good rear angulation and correct tail set. Moved with drive.

2 Montell's Culverwell Miss Demeanour , tri bitch with stronger head than 1. Good lay back of shoulder and adequate reach of neck. Straight front and well ribbed up. Well bodied and plenty of bone. Moved with drive. Shown in good coat and really hard condition.
3 Stirk's Ravensett Suzannah via Grakar
Lb (2)

1 Grimsdell's Tattersett Frankel (jw) blue with a lovely feminine head and dark eye. Reachy neck into good layback of shoulder. Straight front. Well ribbed up and with correct sweep of stifle. Moved out well and was true coming and going. Just lost out in the challenge for best bitch because rear movement was not as good as in the class. Shown in very good coat and condition.

2 Tompsett's Radbrooks Kokomo, blue with balanced head and correct ear set and lovely dark eye. Good reach of neck but not the shoulder placement of 1. Well ribbed up and correct rear angulation. Moved true and with drive and shown in hard condition. Not yet the finish of the class winner.
Ob (2. 1 absent)

1 Cooper's Walshaw Frosted Lace among Settrenda, Pretty blue bitch. Feminine head and nice dark eye. Adequate reach of neck and layback of shoulder. Level top line maintained on the move. Well ribbed up and in good coat. Correct rear angulation. Moved true.
Beginners bitch
1 Richecca Baby Doll of Merlycopse, 2 Richecca Fallen Angel
Brace
1 Stirk's bitch brace, moved out well together, presenting a lovely balanced pairing.

2 Mellish's dog brace, started off moving really well together, but one felt that biting his companions ear was in order, which spoilt their symmetry somewhat! Really made me smile, so typically English setter!
Southern English Setter Society Open Show 23/7/2014
My thanks to the Officers and Committee for both the invitation to judge and the warm welcome, and to all exhibitors for the opportunity to assess their dogs.
Michael Winch Yearling Memorial Award (8,2)

1. Kirsch's Sorbus Hugo Boss. Orange belton dog of 21 months. Pleasing lean head with dark eyes . Clean outline with good length of neck, straight front, and level top line which he held on the move. Well-boned and muscled, very well presented and in good coat.

2. Oliver's Wansleydale Faerie Queen at Bramstorm. Promising 8 months orange bitch, with lovely outline when stood. Pretty head and expression from dark eyes. Well-angulated, well-sprung ribs and good tail set. Neat feet. Really liked her but she was giving her handler a hard time today.
3. Hodge's Lakecastle Tomo
Lesley Allan-Scott Open Memorial Award

1. Whittington's Juldeane Excalibur ShCM. Blue belton and tan dog with pleasing masculine head and dark eye. Presented a clean outline with straight front, level topline, ribs leading well back and correct tailset. Moved true and with style.

2. Oliver's Bramstorm Walk the Line. Substantial dark blue belton and tan dog with masculine head and expression. Strong round bone, short-backed and well ribbed. Well-angulated fore and aft. Moved steadily with good width behind.
3. Tompsett's Radbrooks Kokomo.
Kay Stephenson

pages.title: open show critique 2015
blocks: Southern English Setter Society 19th July 2015
Puppy Dog 1st Hollands Couldoran Speckled Wood 9 month old orange. Reasonable angulation front and rear, good depth throughout, well coated for age. Moved steadily.

Veteran dog (5) 1st Wrights Sh Ch Fishwick Dancing Lad. Pleasure to go over this 9 year old. Looking really well today. Still holding his elegant outline. Balanced head with dark eye and melting expression. Lean neck into well laid shoulders. Excellent spring of rib with lovely bend to stifle. Good width of second thigh to give him adequate drive round the ring. Moving out well and enjoying his day.
2nd Tuckers Walshaw Moonstorm JW. Lots to like about this blue boy. Lean head. Well angulated front and rear just not moving as positively as 1 today.
3rd Woods Swannery Magical Moment.
Junior Dog (2,1) 1st Hollands Couldoran Speckled Wood
Yearling Dog (1,1)

Novice dog (4,2) 1st Hodges Lakecastle Tomo Nicely balanced orange. Well off for bone. Has good depth throughout. Lean balanced head with super reach of neck with no signs of throatiness. Would prefer more return of upper arm. Nicely presented.
2nd Hollands Couldoran Speckled Wood
Graduate dog (2,1) 1st Hodges Lakecastle Tomo

Post Graduate dog (3,1) 1st Trigwells Hannahdene Danny Boy. Super glamour orange, all male. Now really coming together. I love his lean head and super soft expression. He has a super balanced outline, strong level topline. Tidy feet. Moved enthusiastically with drive. Reserve best dog.

2nd Tompsetts Radbrooks God Only Knows. Again another youngster who is finally coming together although he really doesn’t do himself any favours! Balanced outline with solid level topline. Straight from with elbows well tucked in. Short coupled with strong, muscled hind quarters. Just preferred the head of 1.

Limit dog (3,1) 1st Croft & Littlechilds Ravensett Royal Legacy With Thistlesett. Very glamourous, well coated blue. Impressive, balanced outline and has excellent angulation front and rear. Good reach of neck. Short coupled with good width to his second thigh. Unfortunately today was not moving as well as I have seen him, which cost him top honours.
2nd Birch & West Hightides Gingerbread Man. 4 year old orange. Correct lean head with dark eye giving a lovely soft expression. Good length of neck into reasonable shoulders. Level topline.

Open dog (3) 1st Pitts Wandsfell Don’t Quote Me. Just coming upto 3 and he is starting to really look the part. No denying he is a male but he has the elegance I was looking for. Balanced throughout with Excellent bone. Dark eye with the softest expression. Has excellent spring of rib with depth to it. On the move he really came to life. Driving from behind with super length of stride he covered the length of the ring easily. Best dog.
2nd Woods Swannery Magical Moment. 7 year old blue. In excellent coat & condition. Slightly heavier in head than 1 but moved out well.
3rd Youngs Decoverley Sundance To Brookedge.
Beginners Dog (3) 1st Hodges Lakecastle Tomo
2nd Peads Sparsett Hembury Explorer Of Lakeview. Tri dog 6 years old. Well coated. Plenty of bone with level topline which he held on the move.

Minor Puppy bitch (1) 1st Gwilliam & Bozier Victoriaview Primrose. 9 month. Pretty tri girl with lean head, dark eye. Straight when viewed from the front. Well presented. Just a bit apprehensive on the move today.

Puppy bitch (3) 1st Thackers Mandyset Tell No One. Nicely made orange. Small frame but everything is in proportion. Well bodied for her age. Well angulated front and rear. Moved with drive from her well developed hind quarters. BPIS.
2nd Feericks Sunrush Moonlight N Roses. Blue bitch, larger frame than 1 but well proportioned. Dark, correct shaped eye. Reasonable angulation front and rear, nice spring of rib. Moved ok.
3rd Gwilliam & Bozier Victoriaview Primrose.
Veteran Bitch (0)

Junior bitch (3) Williams Bournehouse Spring Violet. Very well developed blue. Pretty head and expression. Liked her overall balanced shape. Level topline leading to excellent tailset (lacking in many) super front & rear angulation. Good, tight feet.moved out well.
2nd Thackers Swannery Blue Rose. Very feminine head on this young blue. Liked her excellent reach of neck. A little long in loin and tended to dip her topline a little today.
3rd Thackers Mandyset Tell No One
Yearling bitch (2,1)
1st Thackers Swannery Blue Rose
Novice bitch (2) 1st Thackers Swannery Blue Rose
2nd Gwilliam & Bozier Victoriaview Primrose.

Graduate bitch (4) 1st Pitts Wandsfell Don’t Call Me Babe. Just loved this dark orange who oozed quality. So well put together, each part flowing into the next. Long, lean head, darkest of eye. Reachy neck into textbook shoulders. Short coupled, well set on tail. Short from hock to heel. When she moves she displays excellent reach and drive and has a long, easy stride. As sound as they come. Thank you for bringing her. BB & BIS.

2nd Tuckers Walshaw Date With Destiny. Another lovely orange bitch. Prettiest of heads. Balanced throughout, liked her overall depth with plenty of fore chest. Strong hindquarters with decent bend of stifle. Excellent reach in front on the move which earned her RBB.
3rd Williams Bournehouse Starry Night.

Post Graduate bitch (3) 1st Harris Gemsett Ultra Violet. 3 year old blue with sweetest expression. Very well made girl. Liked her overall outline well sprung ribs with great depth throughout. Neat feet. Lacking enthusiasm on the move today.

2nd Dytes Valsett Up N Rosie. Lovely orange bitch full of breed type. Sweetest of heads. Balanced and well proportioned. Level topline with tail in line with the back. In lovely coat and condition and well shown.
3rd Gwilliam & Bozier Pewterspear Piano Rag Of Victoriaview

Limit Bitch (2,1) 1st Tompsetts Radbrooks Sound Of Silence. 4 year old tri. Very well bodied. Straight front, nicely boned. Correct return of upperarm. Level topline. Moved with lots of enthusiasm but footfall not as positive and not the drive of the main winners.
Open (2,2)
Beginners bitch (3) 1st ) Williams Bournehouse Spring Violet
2nd Williams Bournehouse Starry Night.
3rd Thackers Mandyset Tell No One
Brace 1st Gwilliam & Boziers pair of blue girls. Really well matched pair, went round the ring really well together.
Judge Sarah Loakes
SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY - OPEN SHOW - 19 July 2015

I would like to thank the Committee and Exhibitors for giving me this opportunity to assess a lovely selection of quality dogs on a glorious sunny day set in beautiful surroundings at Chieveley in the Berkshire countryside.
Michael Winch Yearling Memorial Award (3)

1. Williams Bournehouse Spring Violet, 17 month B/B young lady, feminine well-proportioned head with good eye and soft expression, balanced in skull and length of muzzle with defined stop and low set ears. Good neck and shoulders with well-sprung ribs for age, level topline and well-angulated hindquarters. She was presented in good coat and condition and moved around the ring with plenty of drive.
Lesley Allan-Scott Open Memorial Award (11)

1.Trigwell & Weller's Hannahdene Danny Boy With Juldeane JW, most handsome O/B boy almost 2 ½ years old who exudes maleness, and is so well-proportioned throughout. Has a balanced head with square muzzle and well-defined stop, with soft expression and dark eye. Good reach of neck leading into well-placed shoulders, good depth to chest with good spring of ribs carried well back, level topline with correct tailset. He has strong bone, standing on good feet and with powerful well-angulated quarters which he used to cover the ground in style. Shown in good coat and condition.

2. Harris's Gemsett Ultra Violet, 3 year old B/B lady presenting a lovely outline when stood with everything in proportion. She has a really attractive head with dark eye and soft feminine expression and with low set ears. Long reach of neck through well-set shoulders, deep chest with a well sprung ribcage, she has balanced quarters with good angulation and bend of stifle. Beautifully presented and in good coat and condition, moved well.
3. Tucker's Walshaw Date With Destiny JW.
Judge: - Graham Stirk (Grakar)

pages.title: open show critique 2017
blocks: SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY.
OPEN SHOW 16th July 2017.
DOGS.
Minor Puppy 0
Puppy 1 (1) absent
Veteran. 2

1. Wood's. Swannery Magical Moment, 91/2 blue, substantial bone, melting expression nice dark Eye, plenty of work in his head, good tailsett and moved well. Presented in lovely condition. 2. Mellish's, Walshaw Christmas Spirit at Monbrec. Covered the ground well in good coat, well set ears and kind expression.
Junior. 2 (1)
1. Oliver's Branstorm Oberon, orange, correct eye and shoulder placement, with good reach of neck. Well ribbed and drove well off his hindquarters.
Yearling.4.

1. Bevan's, Wattlewood Home Before Dark. Dark Tri, moved well once settled, not overly big, dark Eye, good shoulder placement nice tight feet. 2. Davis's, Merleycopse Dream Machine. Well ribbed-up, good ear set and length of muzzle, moved well. 3. Tompsett's, Radbrook Sloop John. 4. Done's, Sweetest Moonlight.
Novice.4
1. Oliver's Branstorm Oberon.

2. Mellish's, Mandyset Don't Stop Me Now With Monbrec, blue, well-ribbed and good length of loin. Dark eye and good reach of neck, nice tight feet. 3. Bevan's, Wattlewood Home Before Dark. 4. Done's, Sweetest Moonlight.
Graduate.1
1. Taylor & Atyeo's, Samelen Harris Tweed. Dark eye with good reach of neck well set ears and typical head, held topline on the move.
Post Graduate. 2

1. Hodge's, Lakecastle Tomo, Kind eye of good shape, good ear set. Well off for bone nicely laid shoulders with good forearm, good positive rear action. 2. Mellish's, Wattlewood Silver Arrow To Monbrec, dark eye and good reach of neck, not the most positive of front movement and moved close behind.
Limit. 5

1. Syke's, Daraquist Barry A Reef. JW, Blue in lovely condition, dark kind eye well proportioned Head, good reach of neck good upper arm and shoulders, well ribbed and good front action, driving well off his hocks, Best Dog. B.O.S 2. Harradine's, Mandyset Leave It To Lewis At Halliana. Upstanding dog, nice eye but heavier in head than I prefer. Well off for bone and good tail set, moved well with typical tail action. 2. Holland's, Shanandi Golden Sunset. 3. Mellish's, Gemsett Pole Position For Monbrec. 4. Bennet's, Mariglen Blue Star.
Open. 4(1)

1. Weller's Hannahdene Danny Boy at Juldeane.JW. Substansial orange in good coat. Nice head, melting expression, well set ears good reach of neck and well laid shoulders, held topline on the move. Res Best Dog. 2.Kirch's, Sorbus Hugo Boss. Orange with dark eye, good bone and tailset, but today to proud of his tail. 2. Mellish's, Walshaw Blinded By Love For Monbrec.
Beginners 1.
1. Bennet's, Mariglen Blue Star. Blue good ear set and eye, a lille heavy in head for me, moved close behind, well presented.
BITCH'S
Minor Puppy. 0
Puppy.1.
1. Loakes, Goldbirch Wings Of Desire, Tri, only puppy on the day. Low set ears good reach of neck. Good shoulder placement. Happy mover and covered the ground well. B.P.I.S
Veteran. 4.

The best and most difficult class to judge. These ladies could have written the breed standard, all worthy of a red card on the day, how the breed has changed this past eight years and dare I say not always for the better! 1.Tompsett's, Radbrooks Kokomo. Dark eye of good shape, well placed shoulders, covered the ground well. Best Veteran. 2. Rockall's, Settrenda Golden Fern At Lesnee. Senior girl of the day, well laid shoulders and for 10yrs still had a perfect bite and moved as straight as a die! 3. Day's, ShCh Mandyset Rumour has It At Decoverly.
Junior. 6

1. Oliver's, Branstorm Tapestry. Lovely shape to her head, kind eye. Well off for bone with good spring to ribs, correct angulation, balanced on the move. 2. Weller's, Ravensett Giselle At Juldeane.JW. Well shaped head and almond shape to eye, nice reach of neck into well laid shoulders, would just like a little more of her and preferred the movement of 1. 3. Loakes, Goldbirch Wings Of Desire. 4. Bozier's, Victoriaview Lily. 5 .Thacker's, Swannery Sweet Dreams.
Yearling.4.

1. Croft's, Merleycopse Dolly Daydream. Blue with good front and nice shape to head, good low earsett .Topline held on the move, good shoulder placement, and reach of forearm. 2. Tompsett's. Bushbane Celtic Heartbeat Of Radbrooks. Good shape to her eye and low set ears, well off for bone, unfortunately overly proud of her tail which spoilt the picture of her on the move. 3. Wilson's wattlewood Gold Don't Rust. 4. Evan's. Miakoda Secret Rainbow.
Novice.6.

1. Tompsett's.Bushbane Celtic Heart at Radbrooks. 2. Loakes. Goldbirch Wings Of Desire. 3. Evans & Anton's, Balvenie Eublyn May. 4. Bozier's. Victoriaview Lily. 5. Davis's. Merleycopse Strictly Tango.
Graduate.5.(1)

1. Day's, Mandyset Oh Boy At Decoverly. Tri,well off for bone. Gorgeous head and dark eye, excellent foreface and stop,well laid shoulders, correct angulation, moved with drive, just wish there was more of her. Res BIS. 2. Thacker's, Swannery Blue Rose. Dark eye and good ear-set, well placed shoulders. Not as substantial as 1 or as good on the move. 3. Bryant's, Phenset Firefly. 4. Taylor & Atyeo, Samelen Golden Taffeta.
Post Graduate.3

1.Rockall's, Settrenda Promise Of Love For Lesnee. Tri, melting expression and darkest of eye. Tight feet, moved straight and drove off her hocks well. 2.Evan's, Balvenie Eublyn May, Lovely head and eye, reach of neck and angulation good. 3 Reeves, Bournehouse Golden Charm.
Limit.2.

1. Sykes, Daraquist Abbi Riginal. Orange of good bone and depth of chest, excellent reach of neck into well laid shoulders. 2. Taylor & Atyeo's, Hazeysunsett Carissimi.Blue, lovely dark eye,not the length of foreface as 1 and too much weight on her shoulders.
Open. 2.

1.Oliver's, Wansleydale Faerie Queen With Branstorm.Orange well presented, lovely head and neck with good shoulder placement, drives well from the rear, nice front action, holds topline well on the move. Best bitch & BIS. 3. Davis's, Richecca Baby Doll Of Merleycopse. Tri well boned, heavier in head than 1, good topline, covered the ground well.
Beginners.2.
1. Bozier's, Victoriaview Lily. Well presented blue, dark eye, good angulation and correct shoulder placement, held top-line when on the move. 2. Thacker's, Swannery Blue Rose.
Janet Neath. (judge)

pages.title: open show critique 2018
blocks: critique
Southern English Setter Society Open Show 15th July 2018

I would like to thank the officers and committee of SESS for giving me the opportunity to judge at their Open Show. Also to the many exhibitors who not only entered under me but also endured the very high temperatures at the show. I considered that the entry was good when compared to this year’s average championship show entry. There were some difficult decisions to be made in the higher classes and also in the challenge for BIS etc.
Minor Puppy Dog (1)
1.Neath’s Albadora Constant Tyde

Promising 61/2 month old puppy who is still very raw. Good front angulation. Good spring of rib and short coupled. Moved well for one so young. Lost out to the Puppy Dog in the challenge for best puppy only because of maturity.
Puppy Dog (2)
1.Full’s Ravensett The Midas Touch at Teignestuary
11 month old orange belton. Very well presented. Masculine head but not overdone. Straight front. Good angulation front and rear. Moved quite well. Best Puppy Dog.
2.Worthy’s Tattersett Big Orange.
Little to choose between 1 and 2 but preferred the movement of 1. Good deep chest and spring of rib. Another promising puppy but lacking maturity.
Veteran Dog (3,2)
1.Mellish’s Walshaw Christmas Spirit at Monbrec
10 and a half year old orange belton just showing his age now but thoroughly enjoying his day out and moving with some drive. Has a lovely dark eye with a gentle expression.
Junior Dog (2)
1.Taylor’s Wansleydale Quicksilver

13 month old light blue belton and tan. Well schooled and presented which one always sees with this owner/handler. Head of good proportions with a dark eye. Good angulation front and rear. Has a good depth of chest. Moved with drive particularly in the challenge for best dog, but just lacking a bit of maturity for the top spot. Reserve Best Dog.
2.Harris and Bridgwater’s Bridgella’s First Edition with Konakakela

12 month old orange belton who is very promising and was unlucky to be up against 1 as he is lacking the maturity of 1. Has good front angulation and spring of rib, well laid back shoulder. Preferred the movement of 1.
Yearling (2)
1.Taylor’s Wansleydale Quicksilver
2.Salmon’s Gillancette Day Dreamer
Orange belton nearly 2 years old. Good forechest and spring of rib. Lean head and dark eye. Has good bone. Preferred the overall balance of 1.
Novice(3)
1.Bridgella’s First Edition with Konakakela
2.Ravensett The Midas Touch at Teignestuary
3.Baker’s Mandyset on the Button
Graduate (3)
1.Oliver’s Bramstorm Oberon

2 year old orange belton who was a bit fidgety when stood to start with but liked his overall balance. Lean head carried high on the move. Elbows well let down with good front angulation. Excelled in rear angulation and has well let down hocks which he used to advantage. The change of handler in the challenge for BIS really got the best movement out of him. Best Dog and BIS.
2.Davis’s Merleycopse Dream Machine
Two and a half year old orange belton in very good coat which was well-presented. Excellent depth of chest and good front angulation. Peferred the driving movement of 1 and his overall balance.
3.Mellish’s Wattlewood Silver Arrow to Monbrec
Post Graduate(2,1)
Mellish’s Gemsett Pole Position for Monbrec

Blue belton of 6 years. Head of good proportions with appealing dark eye and expression. Straight front with good front angulation. Well let down hocks. Very well schooled and although alone, a worthy winner.
Limit (4,1)
Fisher’s Beechanger Dusty Miller

6 year old orange that I have done well before. He is well made and has matured well with much to like. He has a lovely nature. He has a masculine head and good depth and spring of rib. He moved well even though we were getting towards the hottest part of the day.
Jolley’s Anlory Burano via Jolymore

Another orange who is 4 years old. Built on smaller lines to 1. Well presented and handled. Has an appealing dark eye. Straight front with good bone. Good rear angulation. Moved well. Close decision between 1 and 2.
Tompsett’s Radbrooks Sloop John B
Open (5,3)
Mellish’s Walshaw Blinded By Love for Monbrec
5 year old blue belton who has a head of good proportions. Dark eye with appealing expression. He has good bone and good angulation front and rear. Preferred his movement to number 2
Tompsett’s Rabrooks God Only Knows

Blue belton who is longer cast than the winner. Long and reasonably lean head, dark eye. Has good rear angulation. Looked good when stood but his movement let him down today as it tended to be rather erratic. He was probably feeling the heat.
Special Beginners
Merleycopse Dream Machine
Tattersett Big Orange
Gillancette Day Dreamer
Minor Puppy Bitch(1)
Martin and Bozier’s Victoriaview Hollyhock
Just 6 months old very pretty orange belton. Attractive head and expression. She is very raw at this stage but shows promise. Good front angulation and good bone. Moved well for one so young.
Puppy Bitch (3)
Wale’s Wansleydale Magic Rose

10 month old orange belton who has a feminine head with a sweet expression and dark eye. Has a straight front, good angulation front and rear. Has a good depth of chest. Moved well with plenty of drive. Best Puppy Bitch and Best Puppy in Show.
Neath’s Albadora One Dream

Blue belton and tan who is 10 months old. Has feminine head which is long and lean. Dark eye. Short coupled with good angulation. Didn’t give her best performance as I believe she was feeling the heat. Preferred the overall balance of 1.
Beasley’s Wansleydale Amaretto
Veteran Bitch (4,2)
Day’s Sh Ch Mandyset Rumour Has It at Decoverly

9 year old orange btch who showed very well given her age and the heat. She moved with plenty of reach and drive, in fact she was the best mover on the day! Has a feminine long and lean head with appealing expression. Good angulation front and rear. Very well presented. A credit to her owners. Reserve Best Bitch and Best Veteran in Show.
Tompsett’s Radbrooks Sound of Silence.

Blue belton and tan who is nearly 8 years old. Well presented. Has a feminine head of correct proportions and dark eye. Has good rear angulation but she lost out on movement to 1 as she was feeling the heat.
Junior Bitch (3,1)
Henry’s Beechanger Velvet Crab

One that I have admired from the ringside. 15 month old blue belton and tan. Very smart and well presented. Good head. Slightly arched neck leading to well laid shoulder. Straight front, good angulation and plenty of bone. Soft feminine expression. Movement a little erratic as she too was feeling the heat.
Bryant and Hollis’ Phenset Sparks will Fly
13 month old blue belton. Long lean head of good proportions with an appealing expression from her dark eye. Well let down hocks enabling her to move well with plenty of drive.
Yearling (1)
Baker’s Mandyset I Will Survive

Orange belton who is nearly 2 years old but still looks rather immature. Has a long and reasonably lean head. Good rear angulation. It was difficult to assess movement as she moved rather erratically.
Novice (2,1)
Victoraview Hollyhock
Graduate (4,1)
Oliver’s Bramstorm Tapestry
Light blue belton and tan who has an overall smart and balanced appearance. Soft feminine expression. Long lean neck leading to well placed shoulder. Straight front, well off for bone. Moved well.
Stirk’s Mariglen Night and Day over Grakar

Blue belton and tan who is built on similar lines to 1. This was a close decision, but preferred the firmer topline of 1. She has a lovely dark eye. Good bone and good angulation front and rear. Well presented and handled.
Davis’s Merleycopse Strictly Tango
Post Graduate (6)
Taylor’s Wansleydale Margarita
Orange belton with a head of good proportions being long and reasonably lean. Very smart and balanced appearance when stood. Good spring of rib, body of moderate length with short back. Moved well.
Reeve’s Bournehouse Golden Charm

Very attractive light orange belton in full coat. Very well presented and handled. Lovely dark eye dark eye giving an appealing expression. Straight front. Firm level topline with good tailset and rear angulation. Close decision between 1 and 2 but preferred the more positive movement of 1.
Day’s Mandyset Oh Boy at Decoverley
Limit (2,1)
Oliver’s Wansleydale Faerie Queen with Bramstorm

Orange belton who is so balanced when stood with a straight front, well laid shoulder, deep ribs and correct angulation front and rear. Has an appealing head and expression. Best Bitch, and I thought she might have been my BIS but in the challenge the dog put in the better performance, therefore had to settle for Reserve Best in Show and Best Opposite Sex.
Open (2)
Stirk’s Mariglen Perfect Day for Grakar Sh CM
Blue belton who has a lovely dark eye which gives her that typical expression. Straight front with good bone. Good front and rear angulation, hocks well let down. Well handled and presented.
Davis’s Richecca Baby Doll of Merleycopse
Blue belton and tan who is longer cast than 1, therefore I preferred the overall balance of the winner. She has a lean head, good spring of rib and good tail set.
Special Beginners (4,1)
Martin and Bozier’s Victoriaview Hollyhock
Davis’s Merleycopse Strictly Tango
Ornage belton third in graduate. She has an appealing expression with a dark eye. Long lean head and good spring of rib. Moved better in this class.
Beasley’s Wansleydale Amaretto
Eric Stephenson
SOUTHERN ENGLISH SETTER SOCIETY OPEN SHOW 15 JULY 2018
AWARD CLASSES
MICHAEL WINCH YEARLING DOG OR BITCH

l.TAYLORS WANSLEYDALE QUICKSILVER 13 month blue belton and tan dog.Handsome refined head with correct length and depth of foreface.He has good length of neck, height,frame and an elegant outline.Straight front,level topline and tailset.Well boned and muscled with tight feet and arched toes.Moved accurately both ways.Well presented with lovely silky coat. Hope he fulfills such early promise.

2 Henrys BEECHANGER VELVET CRAB 16 month blue belton and tan bitch.An attractive very substantial mature bitch with superb bone and body,great depth and spring of rib.Straight front, excellent topline and tailset,strong well angulated hindquarters and moved well.Beautiful coat and presentation.
3 Wales WANSLEYDALE MAGIC ROSE
LESLEY ALLAN SCOTT OPEN MEMORIAL AWARD (9)

1,TAYLORS WANSLEYDALE MARGARITA 3 year orange belton bitch in good coat.Well constructed with very good layback of shoulder, straight tight front, correct length of body with good spring of rib.Well angulated hindquarters with width across the thigh. Perfect topline and tailset. Moved with great precision using her tail. Full dentition completed the package.

2.OLIVERS BRAMSTORM TAPESTRY 2 year old blue belton and tan bitch. Preferred her well shaped head with good work and stop. Very flashy eyecatching bitch with good bone and well ribbed deep body.Lovely coat and condition level topline, well muscled and moved well round the ring.
3 MELLISH WATTLEWOOD SILVER ARROW TO MONBREC.
ANNE MONTELL

OPEN SHOW 21th July 2019.
My thanks to the committee for the invitation to judge & for their warm welcome & hospitality. My thanks must also go to my 2 stewards who kept the ring running smoothly.
BIS was Oliver's Bramstorm Oberon, RBIS Day's Mandyset Oh Boy at Decoverly, BV Jolley's Wansleydale Tribute to Jollymore & BP Dennis, Morgan & Harris' Gemsett Ice Cold In Alex at Mariglen.

On the whole mouths were good, but there were a worrying number of gay tails, spoiling the elegant outline on the move. I also found it concerning, that well angulated shoulders were hard to find, especially in the dogs.
PD(1,1ab).

VD (4,1) 1 Jolley & Taylor's Wansleydale Tribute to Jolymore. 9 year old o/b with a pleasing head & dark eye. Strong well padded feet with a well angulated rear. Deep in brisket & well off for coat. Moved out well with a correctly set tail RBD & BVIS. 2 Mellish's Gemsett Pole Position for Monbrec. Dark b/b who could do with a little bit more weight to his advantage. Handsome head & eye, strong bone with a balanced outline, moved well. 3 Holland's Shanandi Golden Sunset.

JD (3,1) 1 Taylor & Atyeo's Samelen Comeback Special. A dark b/b built on a smaller frame. Well proportioned head with lovely dark eye & a correct bite. In lovely coat & condition. Moved with style, but needs time to tighten up in movement. 2 Wright's Sorbus Dance The Night Away, O/b in fabulous coat. Good eye shape & colour, straight front with a well turned stifle. Rather proud of his tail today & movement could of been stronger.

YD (3,1) 1 Worthy's Tattersett Big Orange. Nicely balanced o/b with strong bone & feet, correct mouth with dark oval eyes. Moved out soundly. 2 Salmon's Tattersett Eminent, well grown o/b with a lovely straight silky coat, moved ok with a slashing tail.
ND (1) 1 Jenkinson's Culverwell Spot Of Trouble. Dark b/b, correct dentition, with a nice turn of stifle. Needs time to mature & develop in body.
GD (1) 1 Jenkinson's Culverwell Spot Of Trouble.

PGD (3,1) 1 Mellish's Wattlewood Silver Arrow to Monbrec. This b/b has a long lean head with dark eye & a correct mouth. Well turned rear angulation with a balanced outline while standing. Moved well with a short slashing tail. 2 Salmon's Gillancette Day Dreamer, lovely headed o/b with a happy wagging tail. Taller on the leg than 1 & needs more time to mature.

LD (4) 1 Oliver's Bramstorm Oberon. 3 year old o/b who has the most gorgeous outline, standing & on the move. A handsome dog with a well proportioned long lean head, dark oval eyes, correct angulation fore & rear, long reaching neck flowing into a well set tail. Moved with reach & drive with his head carried high. BD & BIS with a bit to spare, must have a promising future. 2 Taylor & Atyeo's Samelen Harris Tweed. A masculine dog built on a larger frame, lovely coat & condition, with correct proportions, level topline leading to a well set tail. Moved out well. 3 Jolley's Anlory Burano via Jolymore.

PGD (3,1 ) 1 Mellish's Wattlewood Silver Arrow to Monbrec. This b/b has a long lean head with dark eye & a correct mouth. Well turned rear angulation with a balanced outline while standing. Moved well with a short slashing tail. 2 Salmon's Gillancette Day Dreamer, lovely headed o/b with a happy wagging tail. Taller on the leg than 1 & needs more time to mature.

LD (4) 1 Oliver's Bramstorm Oberon. 3 year old o/b who has the most gorgeous outline, standing & on the move. A handsome dog with a well proportioned long lean head, dark oval eyes, correct angulation fore & rear, long reaching neck flowing into a well set tail. Moved with reach & drive with his head carried high. BD & BIS with a bit to spare, must have a promising future. 2 Taylor & Atyeo's Samelen Harris Tweed. A masculine dog built on a larger frame, lovely coat & condition, with correct proportions, level topline leading to a well set tail. Moved out well. 3 Jolley's Anlory Burano via Jolymore.

O (2,1 ) 1 Mellish's Walshaw Blinded By Love for Monbrec. 6 year old b/b, long muscular neck, straight forelegs & neat feet, elbows well tucked in. Just coming back into coat. Flagged a little on the move probably due to the heat.
SBD (2) 1 Worthy's Tattersett Big Orange. 2 Salmon's Gillancette Day Dreamer.
MPB (1 ) 1 Sharpies' Kanietter Saphira. 8 month light b/b with the sweetest of expressions, well angulated quarters with a well developed body for her age. Just needs to gain some confidence.

PB (4) 1 Dennis, Morgan & Harris' Gemsett Ice Cold In Alex at Mariglen. Well grown 9 month o/b who oozes quality & type, well proportioned head with dark oval eye, straight front with correct length & angulation of upper arm, well developed body. So very steady & true on the move with a high head carriage. A promising puppy BPB & BPIS. 2 Oliver's Bramstorm Speckled Wood. At just 9 months this b/b/t doesn't have the maturity of 1 , but has all of the essentials. Very sweet feminine head, long lean neck flowing into a level topline & tail set, moved with confidence. 3 Sharpies' Kanietter Seraphina.

VB (4,3) 1 Day's Mandyset Rumour Has It at Decoverly. What a lovely 10 year old o/b lady enjoying her day out, super shoulder angulation, bone & depth of chest, shown in excellent coat & condition. Moved out with a sound driving action & used her tail to advantage. Sadly lost her drive in the challenge.

Was 4th in quality PB class, balanced outline & in good coat & condition. Moved much better in this class. 3 Evans & Paterson's Gillancette Foxy Lady.
